## 1. Status, Scope, and Authority

This NLSpec defines the Cartulary testing harness subsystem. It is the sole
adopted current authority for the harness mechanics identified in
`authority_boundary`, including owner and row selection, catalog validation,
runner adaptation, retained-evidence auditing, and the existing scheduler,
fixture, service, artifact, cleanup, and verification-gate contracts. Adoption
does not make harness readiness evidence product conformance or Core 05
claim-publication evidence.

No harness test, generator, conformance command, or release command reads,
stats, hashes, or otherwise consumes this file or any other documentation file
as executable evidence. Versioned machine inputs are reviewed projections of
this NLSpec and the applicable product/support specifications; executable tools
validate those projections without parsing their source documents.
OpenAPI release change sets are operational review records: each entry contains
only its semantic fingerprint, compatibility classification, owning component,
and rationale. They MUST NOT copy specification requirement identifiers or use
a requirement catalog as approval authority.

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-001**
This NLSpec owns only harness mechanics: command invocation, owner and row
selection, catalog and runner validation, scheduling, fixture lifecycle,
service ownership, artifact emission, summary emission, retained-evidence
auditing, cleanup, and harness verification gates. Core 00 through Core 04
remain the sole owners of product behavior and product-profile authority. Core
05 remains the sole owner of claim-publication and benchmark-publication
activation.

Owner catalogs, verification contracts, schemas, task-surface inputs, and
execution-topology inputs are reviewed derived contracts. They MUST implement
this NLSpec and their cited product or support owners, but they MUST NOT
supersede either source. Migration trackers and handoffs are implementation
authorities only; they MUST NOT create lasting harness behavior. Guides,
generated outputs, repository source, tests, and retained artifacts MUST NOT
become alternate behavior owners.

Frontend readiness mechanics introduced by `browser-e2e SUITE=visual`,
`browser-e2e SUITE=accessibility`, owner test-family manifests,
`tools/frontend_visual_fixture_registry.json`, canonical row and target results,
and frontend visual/accessibility projections are harness and implementation-
readiness mechanics only. They MUST NOT define Core product behavior, promote
visual or accessibility evidence into product conformance, or activate Core 05
claim publication unless a claim-bearing publication predicate is active.

Superseded command IDs, delivery-phase registries, schemas, artifact
identities, and retained runs are historical investigation evidence after the
v3 cutover. A v3 implementation MUST NOT provide aliases, fallback readers,
dual catalogs, dual writers, or newest-artifact fallback for those predecessor
identities. Historical artifacts MUST NOT close a v3 verification or release
gate. A command ID whose version remains current in Section 4.3 is not
superseded merely because its version suffix is lower than three.

Where repository planning, handoffs, or command descriptions use the phrase "production evidence", the current harness interpretation is release-readiness evidence. Release-readiness evidence is a release gate input, not product conformance by itself and not Core 05 claim-publication evidence unless an owner document later promotes a narrower claim-bearing publication boundary.

Harness graph-cache records under `cartulary.harness_cache_record.v2` are local
acceleration mechanics only. They MUST NOT define product behavior, weaken
target projection or event emission, replace drift/security/readiness/cleanup/
publication verdicts, or be cited as product, release, benchmark, or Core 05
evidence. Same-run sharing is represented by one canonical unit referenced by
several target projections; it has no secondary helper-artifact identity.

Fallow static-analysis mechanics introduced by `frontend-fallow-static`, `.fallowrc.json`, `tools/fallow/*`, `cartulary.fallow_reachability_owner.v1`, and `cartulary.fallow_static_summary.v2` are harness and implementation-support mechanics only. They MUST NOT define product behavior, MUST NOT replace TypeScript, Biome, frontend import-boundary checks, tests, security scans, generated-artifact drift checks, or harness gates, MUST NOT activate Fallow Runtime behavior, and MUST NOT be cited as Core 05 publication evidence.
Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-013, TH-HARNESS-AC-016, TH-HARNESS-AC-022, TH-HARNESS-AC-026, TH-HARNESS-AC-028

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-002**
A harness conformance claim MUST identify this NLSpec version, the exact public Make target or target set under evaluation, the conformance environment from Section 14, and the retained result root/run ID/run root when retained harness artifacts are used as evidence.
Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-015, TH-HARNESS-AC-016

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-003**
The current canonical public invocation surface is Make. In the current profile, a command invocation is canonical only when invoked as `make <target>` from the repository root or through a Make-owned wrapper that preserves the target identity.

Each public target MUST also declare one stable `command_id` using the form `cartulary.harness.command.<name>.v<positive_integer>`. The version is a decimal integer without a leading zero. The `command_id` identifies the command's semantic contract. The Make target name is the current invocation binding for that semantic command. A later adopted NLSpec MAY add additional invocation bindings only when they preserve the same `command_id`, configuration contract, output contract, artifact contract, failure mapping, and cleanup behavior.

Public behavior change gate. Any change to public Make target identity, stable `command_id`, declared schema IDs, retained artifact paths, output shape, failure mapping, or task-surface/topology metadata MUST be specified here before implementation and before generated task-surface or topology outputs are refreshed. Private module movement that preserves those public contracts MAY proceed without changing this gate.
Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-001, TH-HARNESS-AC-004, TH-HARNESS-AC-005

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-004**
Generated files under `internal/gen/**`, `packages/protocol-ts/src/generated/**`, `packages/ui-contracts/src/generated/**`, generated task/schedule artifacts, and generated Make includes are downstream generated artifacts. They MUST NOT be hand-edited and MUST NOT become behavior owners unless a later adopted NLSpec explicitly promotes one of them. `tools/task_surface_owner.json` is the authored machine owner for task metadata and Make binding profiles; `tools/task_surface_manifest.json` and generated Make includes are projections of that owner. `tools/execution_topology_manifest.json` owns execution topology and the closed runtime and resource profile registries only; fixture capabilities are owned by the v3 family schema and broker contract. It MUST NOT embed a second task-surface or test-catalog owner.

Make-owned generation MUST render generated harness state into one private
scratch transaction, validate it there, compare it once, and publish it
atomically only for a refresh operation. A generated renderer MUST NOT create
an implicit repo-local intermediate or publish a partial set of related
artifacts.

When a harness helper or catalog path change affects task-surface, topology, or schedule outputs, the owner input MUST be updated first and downstream artifacts MUST be refreshed through `make generate`. The current verification ladder is `make source-check CHECK=generated` and `make source-check CHECK=schema`. Generated files MUST NOT be edited as the source of truth for helper-path or catalog migration.
Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-001, TH-HARNESS-AC-016

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-005**
Direct package scripts, raw scripts, raw Go/Vitest/Playwright/Biome/Vite/pnpm commands, and tool-specific reports are developer conveniences or child commands unless a public Make target invokes them. Direct invocation of those surfaces MUST NOT be treated as equivalent to a canonical harness run.
Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-001, TH-HARNESS-AC-005


### 1.1 UI review authority

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-022**
UI review is helper-only diagnostic tooling. Its operation success, findings,
product assertions and publication are distinct. This amendment adds no product
or test HTTP route, authentication bypass, product requirement, visual comparator,
or golden promotion path. Presentation remains design/product owned. Executable
inputs never include Markdown or documentation. The adopted amendment identifier
is `ui-review-diagnostics-3`; the harness document and conformance profile remain v3.
This amendment retains the seven review command identities and the v2 result
and receipt envelopes, adopts action-request v3 and renderer-profile v2, and adds
private same-page CLI diagnostics. Minimal control readiness, exact recovery
proof, and weighted parallel work admission remain required.

Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-102, TH-HARNESS-AC-125, TH-HARNESS-AC-126, TH-HARNESS-AC-128, TH-HARNESS-AC-129, TH-HARNESS-AC-132, TH-HARNESS-AC-133

## 2. Purpose, Non-Goals, and Conformance Boundary

The testing harness exists to provide a reproducible repository command surface for local developers, CI entrypoints, coding agents, and release verification. It provides deterministic target selection, bounded output, structured artifacts, explicit service ownership, controlled fixture lifecycle, stable failure classification, and destructive cleanup gates.

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-006**
The harness MUST provide all of the following for public Make targets:

- deterministic target-class and target-selection metadata;
- declared configuration resolution;
- output-mode behavior;
- exit-code mapping;
- retained artifact identity when a target declares artifacts;
- failure classification that separates product assertion failures from harness operational failures;
- cleanup predicates for every destructive operation.
Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-001..TH-HARNESS-AC-017

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-007**
The harness MUST NOT claim provider-specific hosted CI behavior, benchmark publication, release publication readiness, macOS support, Windows-native support, Podman support, or Playwright artifact schema stability unless those areas are explicitly included in this NLSpec's current conformance profile or in a later adopted NLSpec. The current visual-snapshot refresh authority is limited to the helper-only maintenance contract stated in Sections 6, 8, 11, 15, and 17.
Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-012, TH-HARNESS-AC-016

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-008**
Logical scheduler resources are execution constraints inside the harness. They MUST NOT be represented as guarantees about physical CPU, I/O, Docker, database, object-store, browser, or network capacity.
Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-006

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-009**
Adopted Sections 1 through 17 MUST close every current-conformance harness behavior they name. Unbounded delegation to a target, producer, tool, implementation, or applicability judgment is invalid unless the same requirement cites a closed table, schema attachment, algorithm, or explicitly non-normative diagnostic boundary. Generated manifests and generated Make includes MAY mirror a closed contract, but they MUST NOT be the only current-conformance owner for a public harness behavior.

In adopted Sections 1 through 17, `MAY` means true implementation freedom whose divergent realizations remain interchangeable to callers. Acceptance-bearing behavior MUST use `MUST` or `MUST NOT`; this document does not use an advisory normative keyword.
Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-016, TH-HARNESS-AC-029

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-010**
The normative main body in Sections 1 through 17 MUST contain every load-bearing default, bound, omission rule, mapping, algorithm, failure consequence, and acceptance obligation. Appendices and Section 18 MAY contain rationale, examples, sample objects, and research traceability only. A supporting section MUST NOT be the sole owner of current-conformance behavior.
Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-016, TH-HARNESS-AC-071

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-011**
The current normative imported format dependencies are JSON Schema Draft 2020-12, RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme with its verified errata, SHA-256 as specified by FIPS 180-4, and RFC 3339 timestamps constrained by Section 8. A later revision MUST replace an imported dependency explicitly; implementation-library defaults MUST NOT silently change the format contract.
Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-062, TH-HARNESS-AC-066, TH-HARNESS-AC-071

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-021**
Repository test-harness observability is a harness diagnostic subsystem, not
application runtime telemetry. This NLSpec owns harness trace reconstruction,
harness performance metrics, retained diagnostic artifacts, explicit post-run
OTLP export, and the public commands that inspect or export them. The pinned
OpenTelemetry source and protocol baseline is consumed from machine snapshot
and dependency contracts under `contracts/otel/`; this reference MUST NOT
duplicate or silently rebaseline it. Application telemetry scopes, application
`cartulary.module` attributes, deployment telemetry configuration, and the
server telemetry bootstrap MUST NOT become harness configuration or harness
evidence owners.
Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-072, TH-HARNESS-AC-076

### 2.1 V3 execution-control contract

This section owns the complete current execution-control seam. No handoff or
historical tracker supplies additional current requirements. The former
fixed-cap, fixed-shard, phase-scheduler, and fixed-browser-capacity contracts
have been replaced in their original sections; the requirements below state the
shared architecture those sections implement.

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-800**
Every active test-family row MUST declare exactly one `aggregate_placement` from the
closed set `fast`, `standard`, `full`, `release`, or `explicit_only`.
The first four placements retain their ordered aggregate tiers. `explicit_only`
is an exclusion, not a fifth tier. Aggregates and broad owner/suite selectors
MUST exclude it before readiness expansion. Policy dependencies MUST NOT
reintroduce explicit-only rows; such an edge is a configuration error before
provisioning. The catalog MUST reject `minimum_tier`, `default_check`, inferred
placements and implicit fallbacks.

All product Visual rows, Visual-specific support rows and UI-Review rows MUST
use `explicit_only`, including native review qualification. Only the dedicated
`make browser-e2e SUITE=visual`, `make harness-contract SUITE=ui-review`, and exact
`test-slice OWNER=… ROWS=…` selections authorize those rows. Visual validation
includes screenshot assertions and its five support rows. Snapshot update selects
only snapshot-producing rows. `browser-e2e SUITE=all` is retired without an alias.
`test-fast`, `check`, `ci` and `release-check` MUST NOT run Visual or UI-Review.
General schema, catalog, admission, cleanup and shared lifecycle safety checks
remain in their ordinary gates. A passing release gate establishes only its
selected assurance scope; it MUST NOT imply Visual or UI-Review qualification.
No new CI-provider or automatic qualification gate is required.

UI-Review is optional agent-skill tooling, not a product feature. Its qualification
suite MUST NOT be a prerequisite for standard development, product refactoring,
CI or release acceptance. Run it only for explicitly selected qualification of
the UI-review skill infrastructure. Using the skill does not require running its
self-tests. Shared harness safety and evidence checks retain their own owners and
ordinary placements; product visual and accessibility requirements are unchanged.

The current execution topology input is `cartulary.execution_topology.v16`.
The reporting-derived `go_targets` object is retired. Its target-level sharding,
parallelism, safety flags and family-to-binary bindings MUST NOT define execution
policy. Catalog rows and the normalized execution contract own these requirements.
Raw Go aggregate selectors and package inventories are unsupported.
Source completeness MUST be derived from the approved roots in
`cartulary.test_runner_registry.v3`, independently of selected packages or files.
The Go roots are `cmd`, `internal`, `tools/contractgen`, `tools/embedwebassets`,
`tools/objectstoreprobe`, `tools/openapi-operation-catalog`, and `tools/testservices`.
The operation-catalog root owns focused explicit-mutation generation tests; it
does not admit arbitrary tool directories. Every active Go Test function
under the runner build context MUST have exactly one owner-catalog selection;
TestMain is setup, not a selectable assertion. Excluded build contexts, examples,
benchmarks and fuzz targets require human inventory dispositions and MUST NOT
silently satisfy ordinary Go Test coverage. Required unsupported contexts remain
uncovered until an adopted runner contract admits them or equivalent supported
coverage replaces them. New or removed test functions cannot silently escape
catalog closure. Every required Go test context, including harness helper tests,
MUST have an exact owner-catalog selection.
An additional environment or fixture context requires a named assurance boundary,
not a duplicate package-wide selector. Current commands MUST reject prior topology versions and the retired `go_targets`,
`raw_go_aggregates` and `catalog_packages` fields without fallback interpretation.

Frontend completeness covers the browser-unit file patterns declared by the
current Vitest project (`apps/web/src/**/*.{test,spec}.{ts,tsx}` and
`packages/*/src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`, excluding `packages/report-renderer`), harness-node
`apps/web/e2e/**/*.test.ts`, and Chromium Playwright
`apps/web/e2e/**/*.spec.{ts,tsx}`. Helpers without registrations are not tests.
The `renderer-node` Vitest project owns
`packages/report-renderer/src/**/*.test.ts` under the Reporting owner. Its pure
unit rows require frontend installation; its browser integration rows additionally
require the pinned Playwright installation. Integration rows run exclusively in
their test process, reserve browser capacity, and close all test-owned browser
contexts, servers and temporary directories. They do not acquire an application,
database or object-store fixture solely to render generated presentation input.
This context establishes renderer behavior only; sandbox, production packaging
and release qualification require their own evidence. Repository documentation
is not input to these tests; temporary generated presentation source is product
data. The project has a 60-second test deadline and 30-second hook deadline for
bounded cold renderer characterization. These are test-execution bounds, not
Reporting product timeout or performance predicates.
Discovery and selector resolution MUST use the same non-executing parser.
Literal titles, static local constants and supported literal/constant `.each`
tables resolve to exact full titles. Unresolvable test registrations are
configuration failures, not omitted coverage. Registrations MUST be unconditional
module-level statements or statements in literal suite callbacks. Named imports
may alias the runner's `it`, `test`, `describe`, or `suite` interfaces. Bindings
MUST resolve in their declaration's lexical scope; mutable or dynamic title
bindings, conditional registrations, arbitrary callback registration, unknown
registration modifiers and parameterized suite registration MUST reject.
Runner APIs may use simple constant aliases. Computed member access,
destructuring, storage in objects, and passage to arbitrary registration helpers
are unsupported API escapes and MUST reject before setup. Runtime test metadata
and hooks remain distinct from registration; ordinary object property names do
not create runner identities.
The admitted `.each` title grammar is primitive `%s`, `%d`, `%i`, `%f`, case
indices `%#`/`%$`, and primitive named object properties (`$name`), with the
pinned runner's exact formatting. Other formatting tokens, unresolved property
paths or inspected object values MUST reject; neither approximated titles nor
unexpanded templates establish selection coverage. New syntax requires an
explicit parser-contract amendment and parity tests before admission.
Imported `register*Suite` modules MUST expose the named zero-argument exported
function and the importer MUST call it exactly once as an unconditional
module-level statement. Unused, conditional, argument-bearing or repeated suite
calls MUST reject. Runtime profile routing belongs in catalog execution context,
not environment-dependent registration guards.
Playwright logical scenario IDs
and physical project/file/full-title identities MUST both be unique; changing a
scenario ID cannot authorize duplicate execution of the same test. Distinct
assurance contexts require distinct explicitly owned registrations.

Before service or fixture setup, missing, ambiguous, orphaned or overlapping
supported source selections MUST fail with `failure_class=config`,
`failure_reason=configuration_error`, and exit 2. Discovery MUST prune Markdown,
documentation, generated roots/files, dependency trees, vendor trees and test
data before content traversal or file metadata access. It MUST reject traversal
and symlink paths, never execute discovered source, and never broaden beyond
the approved runner roots and source patterns. Human dispositions and external
provenance records remain supporting documentation, not runtime exemptions or
a second selection catalog. Source inventories and catalog totals are derived
diagnostics, never authored completeness targets.

Tier selection MUST precede unit construction and readiness dependency expansion.
An excluded row MUST NOT introduce readiness work; dependencies of selected
consumers remain required. Direct backend and owner selections are not filtered
by aggregate tiers. Consolidation and reviewed changes of test layer MUST retain every required
behavioral assurance under named surviving catalog boundaries. Runner and fixture
semantics MAY change when they are unnecessary for that assurance. The coverage
map MUST identify evidence successors and the additional failure modes retained
at assembled HTTP, browser and rendering layers.

Visual fixture registry validation is one service-free Node operation owned by
`web.design`, selected in the fast gate and exactly once as a visual-suite
prerequisite. It validates fixture identity, metadata completeness, design mappings,
capture declarations and implementation-only fixtures, retaining both metadata
evidence payloads. Rendering, screenshot, layout and focus assertions remain
explicit visual work. Registry validation acquires no application or browser stack.

The four aggregate policies are closed:

| Entry point | Catalog row selection | Additional policy work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test-fast` | `fast` | Readiness required by selected fast work only. |
| `check` | `fast` and `standard` | Blocking source, static, boundary, security and evidence checks, and exactly the three smoke roles in REQ-053. Builds follow selected consumers. |
| `ci` | `fast`, `standard`, and `full` | Inherited blocking policy, production build qualification, advisory analysis and required harness contracts. |
| `release-check` | all four tiers | CI policy plus release, build, compatibility, browser, accessibility, measurement, SBOM, license, and release-evidence work. |

These are alternative scopes. Each invocation compiles one union graph; CI and
release MUST NOT recursively invoke lower gates. There is no comprehensive
tests-only aggregate. Required policy dependencies MAY exceed the ordinary gate
tier only through exact declared row IDs with an owner-backed justification.
An owner-wide selector MUST NOT define a policy dependency. Adding an unrelated
row to an owner MUST NOT expand a gate. Missing or inactive declared dependencies
fail before preparation. Compiler and evidence consumers use the same declaration.

Policy, packaging, and release units are selected by aggregate policy and MUST
NOT masquerade as product test rows. An omitted owner slice selects the complete
active owner inventory. An explicit row slice selects exactly its valid active
rows and is not tier-filtered. Removing a row requires an owner-backed
coverage record naming its surviving rows, preserved assertions, evidence payloads
and applicability limits. Retired identifiers have no runtime aliases. Static
metadata evidence MUST NOT claim browser execution or rendering.
Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-082

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-801**
Every schedulable action MUST compile to one canonical work unit with these
closed logical fields: `unit_id`, `owner_id`, `kind`, `command`, `needs`,
`resource_claims`, `fixture_lease`, `service_dependencies`, `cache_policy`,
`timeout_ms`, `current_run_evidence_outputs`, `reusable_artifact_outputs`,
`failure_policy`, `estimated_work_ms`, and `semantic_digest`. Unit identity is
independent of aggregate target, queue
position, run ID, and invocation timestamp. The semantic digest closes over the
selection, command and declared environment, graph dependencies, resource
profile, fixture lease, service dependencies, cache inputs, timeout, failure
policy, and evidence contract.

The authored work-graph cost model MUST distinguish invocation startup, selected
execution, and invocation cleanup. Startup and cleanup are charged once per
invocation, never once per row. Fixture acquisition, reset and release are charged
at their actual lifecycle boundaries; a separate lifecycle unit and its borrower
MUST NOT both charge the same work. Estimates account for declared child
parallelism and serialization inside package transactions or reusable buckets.
The work-graph owner's Go invocation policy charges startup and settlement
once around the selected row estimates, without dividing serial row costs by
`GOMAXPROCS`. Its closed lifecycle estimates own browser resets, target
finalization, measurement finalization and immutable performance-fixture
preparation. Browser cohort estimates charge their consuming preparation,
selected execution and cleanup once. Packing reserves existing acquisition/reset
and release bounds before lane placement; neither a separate reset unit nor a
second startup estimate may charge the same work. Runtime preparation records
whether a fresh allocation was initialized or a retained mutable allocation was
reset. The browser topology's invocation policy continues to own coordinator
startup/cleanup, separately from the existing lifecycle estimates. Moving reset
into cohort preparation MUST NOT increase any stage or product-runner deadline.
Qualified retained observations may inform a reviewed authored estimate; they
MUST NOT alter a running plan. Resource claims cover the coordinator and its
children, including bounded cleanup headroom, without raising ceilings to hide
avoidable execution work.

Private operation policy MAY declare `timeout_ms` within the work-unit schema's
positive integer bounds; omission uses the work-graph owner's default. The
compiler MUST reject invalid declarations before preparation and bind the
resolved timeout into semantic identity. An assertion that executes a complete
aggregate gate requires an envelope for that selected workload. The human and
machine full-`check` output assertions use 1,800,000 ms; ordinary operations retain
the 600,000 ms default. This outer envelope does not replace child test,
readiness, cancellation or cleanup deadlines.

`timeout_ms` bounds dispatched work, not capacity queue residence. Graph and
native host-capacity queues MUST remain governed by invocation cancellation;
neither may spend or independently apply a selected unit's execution watchdog
before that unit acquires admission. A reset-phase watchdog cannot classify
the consuming cohort's capacity wait as a reset failure. Once
admitted, existing execution, fixture readiness, reset-stage and settlement
deadlines remain unchanged. Cancellation MUST withdraw pending requests and
settle provisional logical ownership; impossible claims still fail before launch.

A unit resolved from a populated fixture profile also contains
`fixture_profile_id` and `snapshot_key`. Those values participate in its
unit identity, command environment where consumed, dependencies, and semantic
digest. Omission is valid only for a unit with no populated fixture profile.

Equivalent direct, aggregate, leaf, and owner-slice selections MUST produce the
same unit IDs and semantic digests. One semantic unit MAY contribute to several
target projections in one graph but MUST execute no more than once. Unknown IDs,
missing dependencies, cycles, unsupported resource names, infeasible claims,
unknown fixture capabilities, unknown cache profiles, or incomplete output
contracts MUST fail before child work.
Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-083

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-802**
One graph compiler and one scheduler facade MUST serve public, leaf, direct,
aggregate, and owner-slice selectors. The scheduler MUST:

1. capture one immutable host-capability snapshot;
2. rank each ready unit by qualified work plus longest estimated downstream path;
3. admit the highest-ranked resource-fitting unit with stable `unit_id` ties;
4. backfill with any lower-ranked fitting unit without reserving unheld resources;
5. add elapsed monotonic time since first eligibility, rounded down to the
   authored aging quantum, to effective rank so backfill cannot starve work;
6. block descendants of failed required predecessors while continuing only
   independent work permitted by target failure policy; and
7. on cancellation, stop admission, terminate owned process groups, release or
   destroy leases, and publish a partial non-success summary.

One monotonic time snapshot MUST serve each admission decision. Dispatch count
MUST NOT increase waiting age. Warm fixture affinity MUST NOT precede effective
rank or the stable unit-ID tie-break; reuse is a fixture lifecycle decision.
Required build dependencies MUST remain explicit and no target-specific priority
may replace critical-path ranking.

The authored graph, qualified cost model, capability snapshot, and capacity
override declaration MUST determine admission reproducibly. Live self-tuning is
outside v3. A scheduler family, shell loop, or nested Make invocation MUST NOT
encode a second scheduling policy.
Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-084

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-803**
Physical allocations MUST retain resident capacity until exact cleanup proves
release. Logical borrowers reserve only their additional active claims; the same
allocation MUST NOT be charged twice. Resident claims do not authorize
`host_activity`. Acquisition, execution, reset, health inspection and cleanup
require active admission through the existing native owner. Owner-process death
alone MUST NOT retire a resident container reservation. Allocation identity and
durable recovery proof MUST survive until settlement. Admission transactions
MUST NOT invoke Docker or other external operations while holding their mutex.
An idle allocation with no remaining compatible consumer is retired first; other
necessary evictions use stable logical allocation keys across renderers and
application stacks. Random allocation identifiers MUST NOT determine ordering.
Cleanup retains bounded drain entitlement.
Admission MUST leave capacity for the bounded cleanup process after active work
drains; resident memory and process occupancy cannot consume that entitlement.
Persistent local services retain their own durable reservation. Attaching runs
validate it and MUST NOT create another reservation for the same services.
Shared host admission preserves the oldest request's priority while independent
active work drains. Later fitting work MUST NOT repeatedly bypass that waiter.
Backfill is permitted only when resident pressure would still prevent admission
after independent active work drains, so existing-resource consumers can make
progress. Required ancestor claims remain charged. Exclusive waiters retain
their activity fence. A renderer borrower MUST retain one pending host-request
identity and its original queue priority across capacity misses. A miss grants no
active or prospective capacity. Before waiting again, ordinary and dedicated
renderer borrowers MUST return their logical slot and provisional application-stack
pin; waiting for a renderer slot MUST NOT pin an idle application stack. Before
every admission attempt, the owner MUST reacquire logical ownership and rebuild
all resident references because pressure retirement may have replaced a physical
generation. Only ungranted requests may refresh resident references; owner, parent,
mode, active claims and capacities remain immutable. Granted requests and their
physical references MUST NOT change. Cancellation or preparation failure MUST
settle the pending request and yield logical ownership within the existing cleanup
allowance. Admitted active borrowers retain their exact pins until settlement.
This is admission waiting, not a product retry.

A prospective service reservation whose acquisition never began is not a running
allocation. When its final consumer becomes terminal, the owner MUST release its
pending residency proof without requesting physical drain admission. Attempted or
uncertain acquisitions retain the normal admission and exact-cleanup requirements.

An unstarted renderer slot is provisional logical ownership, not an established
physical profile or trust generation. Compatible resident quantities MAY be reused
when that slot is reassigned before any physical acquisition begins. Reassignment
MUST NOT allocate another physical generation, publish a physical retirement, or
create another durable residency proof merely because a queued consumer has a
different runtime profile, lifetime policy or diagnostics setting. The existing
lane limit bounds provisional slots. A changed resident claim must fail closed;
physical acquisition binds immutable profile/trust/diagnostics identity, and any
attempted or uncertain acquisition retains normal quarantine and exact cleanup.
After acquisition begins, existing physical compatibility and retirement rules
apply without exception. Unstarted cancellation must not leave a slot or capacity
claim unavailable to subsequent work or exact finalization.
Ordinary admission MUST distinguish temporary active-work contention from a
capacity shortage that remains after independent active work drains, retaining
required ancestor activity claims under the same weighted accounting. It MUST NOT retire a
reusable renderer for a shortage that its resident resources cannot relieve.
Capacity-driven eviction retires one eligible allocation, awaits exact settlement,
then re-evaluates admission; slot exhaustion likewise retires only the slot needed
for the next allocation. The internal retirement query SHALL identify the exact
resident records that the proposed cleanup releases, including generation identity,
claims and ownership reference. Quantity-only queries are unsupported. The native
owner SHALL evaluate persistent deficits twice with the same weighted algorithm:
with the current residents, and with only that exact set removed. Both evaluations
retain required ancestors and every prospective allocation the pending request
would still acquire. Eligibility requires a strict reduction in at least one
persistent deficit and no increase in any deficit; eliminating every deficit is
not required. Volume retains its non-additive semantics. Unknown, duplicate,
changed, or stale resident identities SHALL fail validation. Evaluation grants no
cleanup authority and releases no capacity.

The fixture owner SHALL include an exclusive PostgreSQL generation in a stack's
release set only when that exact stack cleanup settles it. Shared, measurement-owned
and unrelated service generations SHALL NOT appear in pressure release sets.
Idle renderer and stack candidates SHALL be considered together: first those with
zero compatible remaining consumers, then pressure-relieving reusable candidates
ordered by stable logical allocation key. Renderer-slot exhaustion remains a
separate renderer-only constraint. Before cleanup, borrower exclusion, provisional
pins and the exact generation SHALL be revalidated. Successful cleanup releases
only its exact claims; failure retains claims, recovery authority and quarantine.
No capacity, resource-profile quantity, ranking, fairness or browser-lane change
is implied by this retirement policy.
Idle ordinary application stacks are also eligible when their physical claims
relieve persistent pressure. Retirement MUST preserve borrower exclusion and
force fresh database and leaf-key acquisition for subsequent consumers.
Installed lifecycle tests that launch dedicated infrastructure MUST declare its
peak resource envelope before parent execution. Weighted descendants consume
that entitlement without double charging; unrelated retained allocations remain
charged. Such tests MUST NOT request unused outer managed-service dependencies.
Lifecycle tests of independently reserved persistent services MUST instead
declare only their control-process envelope. Their physical service claims
remain with the persistent owner; they MUST NOT also appear in the enclosing
test's claims. Cases using these different ownership models MUST be separately
selectable and independently admitted.
Before exclusive allocation, the physical owner MUST retire idle ordinary
renderers and application stacks. An active borrower MUST never be evicted.
Later stack consumers acquire a fresh ordinary database or their sealed fixture
snapshot with fresh leaf keys under the same trust scope. Existing reset
operations and independently accounted isolation-contract boundaries remain mandatory;
mutable application state MUST NOT be carried between groups to enable reuse.

The capability snapshot MUST record effective CPU set, memory bound, process
limit, writable-volume availability, port-lane availability, and declared
service readiness. Resource profiles declare CPU tokens, memory bytes, IO
weight, process slots, and scarce service capabilities. Capacity for a unit
class is the minimum capacity implied by every claimed dimension. Missing or
invalid data fails safe to one lane for the affected scarce resource.

Family-specific capacity-forwarding variables are unsupported after cutover.
Graph-backed public commands MAY accept one schema-validated capacity override
declaration file through `CARTULARY_HARNESS_CAPACITY_OVERRIDE`; inline JSON is
unsupported. Every override is range checked and recorded with its source in
the run manifest. `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS` applies only to matching runner units
and its effect MUST be represented by their resource claims. `BROWSER_LANES`
is a logical upper bound, not admitted host capacity. The authored topology owns
its default of four and maximum of six. Six is opt-in. Host-bounded service and
port capacities MUST follow REQ-353, including the independent resident service
reservations; increasing lane count MUST NOT bypass admission or cleanup
headroom. `PLAYWRIGHT_WORKERS` is retired and explicit
public use MUST fail closed. Each scheduled group has exactly one worker,
worker index offset zero and one prepared worker account; inherited inputs
MUST NOT widen those values.

The resource profile selected by `resource_profile_id` is the sole owner of a
unit's base numeric claims. Runner-local default claim tables are forbidden.
The execution topology MUST also own one minimum resource-claim map for every
admitted service dependency. Compilers merge each declared dependency into the
selected profile with maximum-per-resource semantics, so a profile MAY reserve
more than the service minimum but no path may reserve less. Browser PostgreSQL
intensity and object-store admission claims follow this same rule; they are not
compiler constants.

Telemetry MUST expose requested and resolved capacity, peak use, saturation
intervals, queue duration, blocking resources, and actual resource holders.
Waiting evidence MUST distinguish fitting work awaiting rank selection, resource
blocking, exclusive-work blocking, and scheduler stop. A change in blocking
reason or relevant holders MUST close the old wait segment and open its successor
at the same decision boundary. A unit has at most one open segment; ordered,
nonoverlapping segments MUST exactly cover eligibility through admission or
terminal cancellation. Eligibility occurs once. Canonical accounting, live views
and retained readers MUST agree; initial holders MUST NOT be attributed to later
intervals without evidence. Existing output bounds and explicit truncation remain.
Host-admission observations MUST distinguish graph reservations, granted active
host claims, charged resident allocations, ungranted prospective allocations,
and measured consumption. The native admission evaluator is the sole producer
of decision facts; diagnostic readers MUST NOT duplicate its accounting policy.
REQ-857 defines the optional bounded observation contract. Diagnostic failure
MUST NOT affect admission decisions, product outcomes or cleanup authority.

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-804**
Ordinary PostgreSQL and object-store consumers MUST attach to an explicitly
published owner generation. `s3test.StartShared` MUST reject absent or incomplete
attachment instead of provisioning a service. Explicit owned-service APIs remain
available for service lifecycle tests. Borrower cancellation MUST NOT destroy
the service owner. Compatible ordinary PostgreSQL consumers share one initialized
service and immutable migrated template per provisioning identity only when their
explicit cluster scope is shared. Database isolation and PostgreSQL cluster
isolation are separate capabilities. Every catalog row declares
`postgres_isolation` as `none`, `shared`, or `exclusive`. Broker-provided
PostgreSQL dependencies require shared or exclusive scope; none means there is
no broker PostgreSQL attachment. Existing explicit lifecycle owners retain their
own exclusive services and declared physical claims without a duplicate broker
service. Missing or contradictory declarations fail before provisioning.

Browser allocations (including measurement), migration/role/cluster-state
mutations, checkpoint observations and lifecycle/deadline assertions require
exclusive scope. Scope MUST include fixture provisioning and retirement, not only
product assertions. A dedicated database created and dropped for a selected test
or work unit requires exclusive cluster scope: DROP DATABASE checkpoint work is
cluster-wide even when all product mutations are database-local. Shared scope is
permitted for approved rollback buckets without per-test database replacement or
drop, provided assertions and mutations are database-local and do not observe
cluster lifecycle or deadlines. Their owner-provided initial provisioning and final
physical service cleanup remain admitted, accounted and bounded; rollback failure
still poisons the bucket. An exclusive generation belongs to one fixture lifetime:
one browser lane/allocation or one non-browser work unit; the databases within
one Recovery fixture may share that fixture's generation. Unrelated allocations
MUST NOT attach to it. Measurement retains its dedicated quiet lifetime.
The measurement cluster and clone ordinal belong to the exact snapshot builder
unit, fixture profile and snapshot key. A consumer's runtime profile may differ
from the builder policy and MUST NOT redirect the consumer to another cluster.
Browser trust, renderer and session compatibility still use the consumer runtime.
Partial snapshot identity or shared snapshot scope fails before provisioning.

The existing native fixture owner owns both scopes. Attachments bind physical
generation, provisioning and template identity, scope and owning allocation.
Shared attachments cannot satisfy exclusive requests. PostgreSQL, object-store
and renderer ownership remain independent; binding composition validates exact
private descriptors rather than silently replacing ambient credentials. No
additional service manager, scheduler or implicit provisioning fallback exists.
Each physical cluster retains its authored memory/process/port/PostgreSQL/volume
claims through idle residency and physical cleanup. Startup activity is charged
separately, shared residency once, and exclusive residency once per generation.
Impossible claims fail before launch; nested startup cannot wait for capacity
held by an incompatible enclosing claim. Cleanup headroom remains available.
Partial acquisition, publication failure, cancellation and owner loss retain exact
recovery proof. A provider that has acquired physical ownership MUST return that
partial ownership to the existing fixture broker even when startup fails. The
broker owns cleanup and quarantine; local cleanup must not hide an unsettled
allocation or omit its exclusive service retirement. The broker MUST durably publish
its minimal allowlisted recovery environment before launch intent. Success-only
service bindings MUST use a separate disposable output; validating those bindings
and atomically refreshing recovery authority precede consumer admission. Failed
startup or loss during binding publication MUST NOT erase pre-ready authority. Primary startup and secondary
settlement failures remain distinct. Uncertain settlement cannot readmit a generation. Quarantine takes
effect when any borrower invalidates a generation, including while siblings remain
active. No replacement for the same allocation affinity may reach its service
binding until the prior physical generation is settled. Unrelated affinities remain
independently admissible under ordinary capacity accounting. Cluster scope
isolates PostgreSQL control-plane state, not shared host CPU or storage devices.
Dedicated clones and fresh migration databases preserve their database contracts.

A browser allocation owns the combined service binding and its object namespace.
It MUST clear that exact namespace before releasing its dependency on the
object-store owner; PostgreSQL termination cannot stand in for object cleanup.
Recovery uses the allocation's saved binding and environment, with both physical
owners retained as dependencies. A PostgreSQL-only measurement builder may later
serve browser clones without acquiring an extra PostgreSQL generation or making
the PostgreSQL owner responsible for the independent object-store lifetime.
Self-owned lifecycle and installed-package selections retain their existing
physical owner and bounded claims; the broker MUST NOT create an unused service
or duplicate its resident reservation merely because a service dependency is
listed. Their scope declaration still constrains compiler compatibility.

The `volume` claim retains the existing writable-root capability (maximum of
concurrent claims), not a count of physical disks or an I/O isolation promise.
Native dispatch and both canonical evidence projections MUST use the same
maximum across active volume claims, including overlapping starts and releases.
Memory, process, port, and PostgreSQL claims remain additive across physical
clusters. Capacity ceilings are unchanged.

The physical PostgreSQL owner MUST initialize fixed roles, deployment logins,
memberships and parameter privileges exactly once after service readiness and
before publishing its generation. Failure publishes no usable capability.
Fresh database preparation owns extensions, schema ownership, extension ACLs
and default privileges. Ordinary template clones MUST NOT replay those operations
or acquire a cluster-wide provisioning lock. Clone creation and database-specific
ACL finalization share target-scoped catalog admission: CREATE uses `WAL_LOG`
with connections disabled, then database grants are established and connections
enabled before publication. A failed finalization cleans only a proven-created
target. The service generation and digest of the executed provisioning policy
are mandatory attachment identities; template identity also binds the migration
digest. Canonical consumers attach explicitly and MUST NOT start or repair a
service when attachment is absent or incompatible. Explicit lifecycle fixtures
may own dedicated services. Core 04's per-connection identity and TLS admission
remain mandatory on every new and recycled connection.

Renderer infrastructure is orthogonal to fixture capabilities and managed-service
dependencies. Its closed requirement is `none`, `pooled`, or `dedicated`. One
native run owner lazily provisions up to the resolved `BROWSER_LANES` pooled renderer slots, subject
to capacity admission. The compatibility key binds run, runtime profile,
renderer/image/package identity, immutable public trust digest and launch options;
it excludes suite name. A slot has at most one group borrower. Every borrow binds
run, unit, allocation and generation and emits independent row evidence. Physical
ownership is journaled before creation. The group owns its clients, never the
shared container. The compiled graph SHALL register every selected unit with the fixture owner before
admission, including units with no fixture requirements. The owner SHALL derive
consumer keys from the same compatibility functions used for allocation reuse;
reporting owner and unrelated catalog rows SHALL NOT influence them. Stack identity
SHALL bind capability, PostgreSQL scope, affinity, runtime profile, browser stage,
fixture profile, snapshot/builder identity and declared services. Renderer identity
SHALL bind the run-owned immutable renderer/trust configuration, runtime profile,
lifetime policy and diagnostics mode. Dedicated physical renderers have no future
reusers; unstarted provisional slots retain their existing reassignment contract.

| Terminal notification | Required accounting |
| --- | --- |
| passed / failed, including failure before runner launch | Consume the unit once after any active borrow has settled or quarantined; do not invent a borrow for pre-launch failure. |
| skipped / cached, runner not started | Consume the selected unit without inventing a borrow. |
| cancelled, started or never started | Consume the unit exactly once; cancellation does not release physical ownership. |
| Identical duplicate | Return the original accounting result without decrementing again. |
| Unknown unit, invalid disposition, contradictory duplicate | Fail required lifecycle validation; do not change counts. |

Terminal accounting SHALL occur for every selected graph unit, including dependency
failure, cache hit, cancellation before host admission and required-publication
failure. Remaining consumers SHALL never be negative. A healthy idle allocation
MAY remain while compatible consumers remain and capacity permits. Zero-consumer
idle allocations SHALL promptly enter admitted cleanup. Terminal notification MUST
NOT block the graph event owner on physical cleanup. The existing fixture owner
SHALL own bounded cleanup dispatch and join its outstanding cleanup before final
resource reconciliation; this introduces no scheduling policy or admission bypass.
Cleanup failures SHALL reach the required finalization result and preserve earlier
product failures. Shared service dependencies and measurement generations may
retire only after their complete consumer roster and dependent allocations settle.
External persistent owners retain their independent authority. A standalone dedicated
review owner SHALL have no future-consumer roster and SHALL retain no reusable
allocation after its sole borrow. Graph execution SHALL require exactly one
immutable registration before admission. Cleanup dispatch SHALL use one worker
and a coalesced wake signal; finalization SHALL join that worker before inventory
reconciliation and reject any registered nonterminal consumer.

The compiler's static release-affinity environment marker and runtime-profile-only
future-consumer counters are retired without fallback or compatibility toggles.
The compiler MAY retain deterministic lifecycle estimates; an estimate is not
cleanup authority. Consuming-cohort reset boundaries, fresh contexts, isolation,
measurement quietness and existing failure policies remain required. No TTL,
cross-run retention or owner-name exception is admitted.

A successful borrow may return only after bounded proof that
the server is alive and client connections, connection-owned browsers and
forwarding listeners have settled. Failure, interruption or uncertain cleanup
quarantines and retires the generation without retrying product work. Physical
attestation occurs once per generation; logical results reference it. Last use,
capacity eviction and run finalization retire resources through the same owner.

Browser fixture authorities belong to the native run/runtime-profile owner.
Signing keys remain in owner memory; each stack receives distinct leaf keys.
Its public root and the exact suite object-store root form an immutable renderer
trust bundle. Trust is never extended in a live renderer. Renderer acquisition copies the admitted
public trust bytes while its caller holds the source stack. The renderer owns
that immutable copy and its capacity reservation independently of service
lifetimes; a cluster's retirement MUST NOT retire another allocation's renderer
or clients through a dependency on live managed services. Foreign-authority and
wrong-hostname fixtures remain required. Recovery after owner loss is cleanup
only. Measurement and UI review use dedicated renderer/trust lifetimes through
the same acquisition primitive. Chromium remains connection-owned and every
test receives a fresh context. Canonical browser execution without a validated
renderer attachment fails; local-launch fallback is unsupported.

One run-scoped broker owns infrastructure readiness and cleanup. It MAY attach
to already managed Postgres and object-store services, but it MUST NOT close a
borrowed resource. Every application stack, browser stack, database, namespace,
port set, and process created by the broker is owned by an explicit lease.

Logical leases and physical allocations have distinct lifetimes. Release of a
logical lease MUST settle once; repeated or concurrent release with the same
disposition MUST observe that settlement, including its failure. Contradictory
repeated dispositions MUST fail rather than change the original operation.
Each physical allocation MUST have one explicit cleanup owner and at most one
cleanup attempt within that lifetime. Callback return values MUST NOT select a
second cleanup operation. A borrowed allocation permits detachment only.
An unhealthy shared allocation MUST immediately leave the reusable index;
remaining borrowers drain before its cleanup, and later healthy releases MUST
NOT restore eligibility. Allocation ownership MUST survive failed publication
and cleanup until settlement or exact resource-owner recovery proof exists.

Browser allocation MUST publish a versioned private acquisition identity before
launch. Its immutable descriptor binds the run, runtime lease, exact managed
suite proof and ready-lease destination. Producer and service process boot/start
identities and exact port leases are journaled before their dependent work is
exposed. Each process launch MUST first publish an immutable launch identity.
The creator MUST record the exact child identity before acknowledging launch;
the child MUST also record it before starting dependent work. An unbound launch
MUST prevent terminal release until its creator proves no child was created or
its exact process group was reaped. Stopping MUST fence new launches; a late
launcher MUST retain its identity and exit without starting its payload.
Confirmed process settlement MUST durably retire that launch's process authority
before a reset replaces the service or cleanup advances to other resources.
Later attempts MUST honor this acknowledgement and MUST NOT signal the retired
identity again. Failed settlement retains its proof for retry. A closed launch
cannot publish another process identity. A validated terminal acquisition receipt
returns its immutable settlement without reacquiring process-control authority.
The ready attachment is not acquisition or cleanup proof. After a failed
or cancelled acquisition, the browser owner MUST reap its producer and settle its
resources, or preserve exact recovery proof and every required service dependency.
A detached service supervisor MUST retain its journaled identity until physical
settlement starts, including when its immediate payload has already exited.
Payload completion alone cannot retire the authority needed to settle descendants.
An adapter given an explicit runtime binding MUST use that binding for process
settlement as well as acquisition and journal updates. Ambient parent-run
identity MUST NOT substitute for that explicit authority.
A missing ready lease MUST NOT establish that nothing was acquired. Resources
owned by the managed suite remain in that owner's cleanup boundary until its
ledger/container finalizer settles; browser retirement does not claim suite
cleanup. Ordinary release shares one settlement; a later explicit recovery is a
separate attempt against the same exact proof.


A suite-service janitor MUST NOT infer abandonment from container age. Other runs retain service ownership until their exact terminal cleanup proof authorizes reclamation. Unproven orphan resources remain subject to their lease-specific cleanup; startup of a concurrent suite cannot remove them. Cleanup evidence identifies the container and its owning run and suite before removal. Browser database/bucket cleanup MUST select only the exact current suite ledger and its validated service bindings. A common run, generated resource name or retired-fixture event from a sibling suite grants no cleanup authority. Abandoned allocations remain subject to their existing exact lease/journal recovery; a new cluster MUST NOT attempt their cleanup through its own bindings.

The fixture capability set is closed to `none`, `postgres_transaction`,
`postgres_dedicated`, `postgres_migration`,
`object_store_namespace`, `managed_process`, and `browser_stack`. Omission is
invalid and there is no implicit template-clone fallback. Failed reset, health,
or contamination proof quarantines and retires a lease. Dedicated databases are
created on demand; asynchronous replenishment and a writable clone pool are
unsupported. A digest-keyed migrated template is valid
only when an owner test proves the same migration chain produced it; every owned
migration chain retains at least one full-chain proof.

Reuse admission requires affirmative settlement of the preceding borrow. Failed,
canceled or uncertain reset, rollback, connection close, cleanup or readiness
MUST remove the resource from reusable indexes before admitting another borrower.
A later successful operation cannot restore that generation's eligibility.
Cleanup preserves its primary failure and exact ownership; uncertain settlement
retains recovery proof. No borrower may interpret missing cleanup evidence as
an empty or healthy resource.
This rule also applies to successive fixture preparations within one Go test
process. Failed owned-database cleanup MUST prevent further preparation on that
process's affected cluster generation, including through an already-held harness
or a released and reacquired attachment. Existing resources may still settle;
new preparation fails with typed fixture evidence, and independently completed
outcomes and unrelated generations remain intact.

Object-store cleanup MUST traverse the exact owned bucket or prefix completely,
reject missing or repeated continuation tokens while traversal is incomplete,
and verify that the exact namespace is empty before reporting success. A missing
bucket may satisfy terminal destruction but cannot admit a reusable bucket.
Batch deletion MUST obey the pinned provider's request limit and check both
transport and per-object errors. Success of a request or pagination termination
alone is insufficient. Reusable buckets additionally pass their mutation
readiness probe. Cleanup remains cancellation-aware and bounded, never deletes
sibling prefixes, and belongs to the harness rather than the production storage
API.

Harness-generated bucket names MUST have exact cleanup ownership reserved before
the create request can mutate the provider. An uncertain create retains that
reservation until terminal cleanup proves destruction; a reservation is not a
successful creation count. The private suite-service journal and resource ledger
use `cartulary.test_services.journal_event.v2` and
`cartulary.test_services.resource_ledger.v2` for this ownership contract. Their
producers and readers cut over together; prior versions are historical evidence,
not current cleanup authority. Package fixtures retain failed generation identity
but never readmit it after failed creation, reset or mutation readiness.

Before publishing an initialized generation's migrated template to any borrower,
the physical owner MUST seal that template and complete one PostgreSQL checkpoint
under the existing bounded provisioning context. This boundary settles the
owner's initialization writes before borrower cleanup can request a cluster-wide
checkpoint. Native self-owned preparation and broker preparation MUST use the
same sealing implementation and provisioning identity. Failure or cancellation
MUST withhold publication and retain exact cleanup authority. No borrower may
perform or repair this owner preparation; attached templates must already satisfy
its versioned provisioning identity. This one initialization checkpoint does not
change normal PostgreSQL checkpoint behavior or authorize per-clone checkpoints,
cleanup retries, longer cleanup budgets or weaker durability settings.

A database copied from a harness template MUST use the pinned PostgreSQL
`WAL_LOG` strategy and complete successful durable CREATE before publication.
PostgreSQL logs the copied blocks and synchronously commits database creation;
the harness MUST NOT add a whole-cluster checkpoint to each clone. Such a
checkpoint unnecessarily couples acquisition to unrelated dirty data and is not
required for WAL-backed durability. Fresh migration databases retain ordinary
creation. Creation success and complete acquisition success remain distinct:
the clone owner MUST receive whether CREATE succeeded, even when admission
release fails. Failed subsequent provisioning MUST delete the proven-created
database with the existing bounded cleanup owner and retain both acquisition and
cleanup failures. Failed CREATE MUST NOT authorize deletion of a pre-existing
name. No consumer receives the clone before its required provisioning succeeds.
This preserves `fsync`, full-page writes, synchronous commit, checksums, exact
ownership, physical deletion and PostgreSQL's normal checkpoint behavior.
Independent acceptance MUST verify durable WAL progress, creation without
checkpoint privilege, template/clone isolation, failed provisioning and existing
cleanup budgets on an owned cluster. Elapsed-time comparisons alone cannot
establish this boundary.

Fixture capability describes broker-owned isolation and lifecycle only. It is
not a declaration of every managed service a helper consumes. Each catalog row
and work unit therefore carries a separate, required, ASCII-sorted,
duplicate-free `service_dependencies` array. The current service-dependency set
is closed to `object_store` and `postgres`; adding a service requires an adopted
topology and schema revision, not a composite fixture capability.

Infrastructure setup MAY use its Section 11 bounded retries on a new lane only when no product
work began and the failure occurred before service readiness polling began.
Once readiness polling begins, its expiry is terminal for that lane and MUST NOT
start a replacement lane. Product test failures MUST NOT be retried by scheduler
policy.

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-805**
The `node-unit` Vitest project owns explicitly named `*.node.test.ts` under
ordinary frontend roots, excluding dedicated harness and report-renderer roots.
The jsdom project MUST exclude those files. Static discovery, catalog project
IDs and runner selection MUST agree without a second per-file environment map.

Compatible Go rows MAY share a process only when their normalized execution
contracts agree: module and exact package, build/runtime environment, runtime
binaries, resolved dependencies, resource claims, fixture capability and profile,
PostgreSQL scope, timeout, cache/failure policy and process isolation. Resolve
these properties for every selected row before grouping; the first row cannot
supply an unproved common contract. Reporting target, owner, family and
verification attribution MUST NOT partition execution or enter its identity.
They remain individual row bindings and reporting projections. Each selected
symbol executes exactly once. Dedicated and migration databases remain per-test;
their exclusive cluster lifetime belongs to the execution unit. Managed-process
and explicitly process-exclusive rows remain singleton invocations. Compatibility
permits sharing; it does not mandate one invocation per partition. REQ-379 and
the sizing policy below determine execution sizes. Go JSON remains authoritative
for row outcomes.

For explicit Go-only `test-slice` selections, a declared positive integer
`GO_SHUFFLE_SEED` MAY vary Go's test execution order reproducibly. It MUST preserve
exact selected symbols, be retained with declared inputs, and participate in
command, work-unit and cache identity. Omission preserves normal runner order.
Invalid seeds and selections containing non-Go work MUST fail before execution.
Inherited compiler flags MUST NOT supply this control. Ordering diagnostics do not
establish completeness independently of authoritative Go JSON outcomes.

Compatible Vitest files MAY share a bounded invocation-local cohort when project,
runtime environment and setup, dependency set, resource/fixture profile, service
dependencies, required owner partitions, evidence class, timeout, failure policy
and isolation policy match. Each cohort starts one fresh coordinator and initially
uses exactly one file worker; scheduler claims cover both. File environments remain
isolated, with normal setup and teardown for each file. Exclusive/process-global
cases remain singleton invocations. A resident test daemon is unsupported.

Reporting owner, family and verification identities MUST NOT independently
partition otherwise compatible Go or Vitest execution. Required owner partitions
MUST be expressed by the applicable runtime, setup/environment, dependency,
resource, fixture, evidence, timeout, failure or process-isolation contract;
the compiler MUST NOT infer isolation from an owner name. Selected rows retain
their individual owner and verification attribution. A mixed-owner Vitest unit
uses `harness.command_surface` as its execution owner; Go units retain
`harness.backend`. These execution owners MUST NOT replace catalog row ownership
in evidence. Owner-specific selection MUST NOT widen to unselected owners.

Selection, compatibility, sizing, admission and reporting are separate
responsibilities. Scheduling items remain indivisible: a Go catalog row with its
exact symbols, a Vitest file with its exact selected titles, and a Playwright row
with its exact cases. A row MUST NOT span execution units. Go rows use the same
bounded first-fit packing rule below, within normalized execution contracts.
There is no speculative shard-count search, wave limit or calibrated cost registry.
Resource admission remains the existing scheduler and fixture broker's responsibility;
estimates never grant capacity. Vitest and browser cohorts retain one worker each.
Browser isolated and measurement rows remain singletons.

Within each compatibility partition, exact file selections are ordered by
descending predicted selected execution cost with stable project/file identity
ties. Deterministic first-fit packing places each selection in the first cohort
whose projected startup, selected execution and cleanup fit the existing work-unit
timeout envelope. An individually oversized selection remains explicit and MUST
NOT cause an increased timeout or additional selected cases. The same packing
rule governs ordinary browser cohorts, using stable semantic row identity ties.
Unit identity, cache semantics and semantic digest bind the exact project, files,
full selected titles and execution policy. Authoritative runner output MUST resolve
every selected row exactly once; missing, duplicate, ambiguous, skipped or
unexecuted cases cannot pass. Partial failure retains independently completed file
outcomes and one invocation cleanup owner. Public row identities and failure
precedence remain.

Vitest selectors explicitly name their registered project. Static resolution maps
each selected title to one exact full test name. Runtime execution MUST use the
pinned Vitest public TestSpecification API with an anchored name filter for each
exact file; a global union of titles is invalid because files may repeat names.
A leaf-name/full-name pair for the same case is overlapping selection.
Unexpected executed cases, duplicate/missing observations, selected skipped tests
and project mismatches cannot pass. An independently completed row retains its
outcome when a sibling selected row is missing or fails. Suite load, setup and
teardown failures affect only their file; unhandled runner errors and invalid
common reports affect the invocation. The existing collector/finalizer path MUST
retain fully settled file observations through interruption or sibling failure.
An unfinished file cannot qualify from a passed test before its teardown settles.
The coordinator MAY submit one exact TestSpecification at a time to its single
worker within the same fresh Vitest instance. A file is settled only after its
public execution promise, successful environment-teardown acknowledgement and
physical worker termination have settled. The pinned runner's execution promise
and module-end callback alone are insufficient. The adapter MUST observe the
public pool-worker lifecycle while delegating execution to the pinned fork worker;
it MUST NOT access or replace private runner state. A teardown error is attributed
to its file, and uncertain termination cannot admit another file. The invocation
owns its diagnostic output stream across worker EOF and coordinator teardown.
Settled file checkpoints use the existing
canonical row publication/finalization path. Each settled file MUST be normalized
and reconciled independently and published once as an immutable
`cartulary.vitest_file_checkpoint.v1` record, bound to the invocation, run, exact
request digest and selected file ordinal. Native report and normalized
observations MUST become durable atomically before publishing that file's rows.
A reader MUST reject foreign, duplicate, malformed, unsafe or selection-mismatched
records; it MUST NOT infer completion from uncommitted temporary files.
`cartulary.vitest_invocation_disposition.v1` records invocation-wide failure,
interruption and final settlement separately from file evidence. An observed
invocation-wide failure MUST be retained before superseding provisional rows.
Independently settled file evidence MUST survive interruption between its atomic
publication and row publication. Row publication MUST preserve an existing
semantically identical outcome and its settlement timestamps.
Observation lookup uses exact project/file/full-title identities. Processing
and checkpoint publication MUST be linear in retained evidence volume, without
cumulative checkpoint rewrites. Terminal cumulative native-report and diagnostic
envelopes are assembled once; all interruption and terminal consumers use the
same validated evidence loader. Intermediate cumulative checkpoints are retired
without aliases or fallback readers.
Invocation-global teardown and
unhandled runner failures remain invocation-scoped and supersede earlier provisional
success when observed; interruption retains independently settled file results.
Even if every selected file settled, an interrupted or failed invocation MUST
retain its enclosing command failure. A private command failure cannot be erased
by an absent disposition failure. A successful command exit without final
invocation settlement is contradictory evidence and MUST NOT qualify.

`cartulary.vitest_invocation.v1` carries the exact invocation-local request,
including per-file row/title bindings and the sole selected project. It is not a
policy registry. `cartulary.vitest_runner_reports.v1` retains unmodified native
JSON report objects keyed by project/file. `cartulary.vitest_failure_details.v3`
identifies completed files and whether final invocation settlement occurred;
interrupted checkpoints cannot masquerade as a complete native report. The
work-graph owner's invocation policy owns startup/cleanup estimates and
coordinator resource claims; the file worker retains the selected resource profile.
All producers and consumers cut over without v2 readers or the former single-file
runner path. Planning and execution both reject ROWS values beyond the existing
4,096-character bound before product execution.
Aggregate cohort selection is read from the invocation's published work-graph
row bindings, validated against its manifest and unit identity; it is not copied
into bounded command arguments or a parallel environment selection registry.

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-806**
Compatible ordinary groups across suites MAY borrow the same physical renderer
without sharing their application-stack affinity or mutable fixture state.
Group/reset boundaries derive from explicit state-isolation contracts in the
existing authored catalog and topology. Filenames and distinct record IDs are
not isolation contracts. Idle ordinary renderers MUST
retire before exclusive measurement admission, and ordinary backfill MUST stop
once that exclusive work is eligible. Measurement keeps its dedicated renderer
through finalization and release; required resident services remain accounted.

Every semantic browser cohort is an ordinary work unit. Compatible rows share
one stack and setup lifetime only when runtime, renderer/trust, resource, fixture,
effective project/configuration, execution policy and declared state scope agree.
Suite, stage, reporting target, owner, family and evidence-attribution labels
MUST NOT independently partition otherwise compatible execution. Each test owns a fresh browser
context and its mutable data. Actor/session state observed or mutated by an
assertion MUST be test-owned; a shared setup account is permitted only for proved
control-plane use. Owned-user administration and identity-scoped listings MAY
share a cohort after that boundary is proved. Actual process-global clock or
registry enforcement and specialized deployment/publication lifetimes remain
isolated where their assertions require that resource boundary. Local browser
presentation faults MUST NOT create a server-global mutation dependency.

Each test MUST have one browser resource owner for its primary and secondary
contexts, independent request clients, actors and acquired session snapshots.
An actor MUST be registered before any login attempt, so a failed login or
snapshot acquisition cannot leave its sessions unowned. Context and independent
request-client acquisition MUST be registered while in flight, before exposing
the acquired resource. Disposal MUST stop admission; an acquisition already in
flight MUST settle under the same owner, including a context that resolves after
disposal begins. New acquisitions after disposal begins MUST be rejected.
Context acquisition MUST inherit the effective project/test settings through the
instrumented browser interface, with explicit scenario overrides preserved.

A scope-owned response barrier has exactly one terminal outcome: `released` or
`cancelled`. Repeated release or cancellation MUST preserve the first outcome.
Disposal cancels pending barriers, including barriers not yet reached by a route
handler. Cancellation MUST NOT approve or dispatch a held mutation. A cancelled
handler MUST settle without falling through to its ordinary request. Route
fetch, fulfillment, abort and drain failures MUST remain observable; broad
exception suppression or matching an error-message string is not cleanup proof.

Disposal MUST return the same completion promise to concurrent and repeated
callers, preserving its original rejection. Its ordered phases are: stop
admission and cancel barriers; settle feature-owned work, including in-flight
job admission and admitted jobs; begin draining every owned page and context
route before awaiting any drain; await all drains; close owned contexts; revoke
owned actors' sessions and verify acquired snapshots through the still-live
provisioner; finally dispose independent request clients. A phase failure MUST
NOT prevent attempts to settle the remaining owned resources. Existing cleanup
deadlines still bound nonsettlement; cleanup failure fails and quarantines the
allocation under the existing cohort policy. The primary test failure MUST
remain primary, with additional cleanup failures reported separately using
bounded operation categories that exclude credentials and private values.

Feature fixtures own their records, job admission and terminal-state observation;
the common browser scope MUST NOT become a feature data or job policy owner.
The provisioner is borrowed control-plane infrastructure and MUST remain usable
through test-session cleanup. A test MUST NOT revoke another test's actor or the
provisioner's sessions. Sessions acquired in a restored disposable deployment
remain in that deployment's boundary and MUST NOT be revoked through the ordinary
deployment's provisioner. Before retiring a specialized fixture runtime or a
resource on which an owned browser context depends, that browser context MUST
settle and close. Independent publication builds retain their existing process
owners and evidence; they may finish while the browser verifies its previously
loaded immutable assets.

Uniquely test-owned durable records MAY remain until the bounded cohort reset.
Assertions over shared listings MUST select owned identities and MUST NOT depend
on database cardinality or a predecessor's residue. Deterministic test identities
MUST execute once per cohort generation. Actor pools, per-test deployment resets,
outer transactions around HTTP work and production deletion APIs MUST NOT be
introduced to substitute for ownership. A multi-case row is shareable only when
every selected case qualifies. Qualification MUST include separate clean forward
and reverse invocations with unrelated users, incidents, audit events and jobs,
using existing harness regression mechanisms without a public shuffle interface.
Local responses establish browser presentation/recovery evidence only; real
owner-defined authorization, persistence, replay, time and cursor enforcement
require independent real-boundary witnesses before predecessor assertions are
removed.

The authored catalog declares each browser row's state scope: `test_owned`

`isolated` requires a singleton; `measurement` requires a dedicated measurement
lifetime. The generated browser manifest describes compatibility partitions,

Each selected row retains its catalog owner and verification attribution; the

use one normalized execution compatibility tuple covering exact project and
