blockers and overlapping phases SHALL NOT be summed as exclusive wall-clock
causes. Resource claims SHALL NOT be represented as measured utilization.


| Timing field | Required calculation and interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| queue_ms | Canonical ready-to-start duration; equals the sum of queue_by_reason_ms values |
| lifetime_ms | Canonical unit terminal time minus start time; cached/unstarted units retain the canonical zero-lifetime convention |
| phases | All canonical intervals for that unit in start/end/name order; duration is end minus start |
| phase_union_ms | Union of phase intervals clipped to unit lifetime |
| phase_outside_lifetime_ms | Full phase union minus the clipped union; includes pre-start cache work where present |
| phase_overlap_ms | Sum of individual phase durations minus their full interval union |
| uncovered_lifetime_ms | Unit lifetime minus the clipped phase union |

Allocation association SHALL include a path unit when it borrows the allocation
or is the recorded retirement trigger. Path-local allocation counts SHALL NOT be
presented as whole-invocation generation counts. Allocation acquisition timing
SHALL bracket provider acquisition. Retirement timing SHALL bracket the owner's
settlement operation, including its required publication. The fixture-broker
monotonic clock SHALL remain independent of the graph clock; readers SHALL NOT
subtract timestamps from those different epochs.

The native fixture observation owner SHALL publish one terminal lifecycle record
per browser_stack allocation in a separately bounded execution-index section,
independent of ordinary execution-record truncation. Each record SHALL contain
opaque allocation identity, logical borrow identities and borrowing unit IDs,
acquisition and retirement intervals, declared monotonic clock identity,
retirement reason, nullable triggering unit and settlement outcome. All values
that cannot be observed SHALL be explicitly unavailable. The owner SHALL record
the actual retirement trigger; readers SHALL NOT infer it from names or timing.
The observer SHALL register each allocation when acquisition begins, independently
of the ordinary record quota. At publication, every registered allocation SHALL
have a terminal record or an explicitly disclosed omission. A missing terminal
observation SHALL make coverage incomplete; it SHALL NOT synthesize a retirement
reason, interval or settlement outcome. Registration and omission identities
SHALL obey the lifecycle section's authored record and metadata bounds.

| Retirement reason | Actual owner decision |
| --- | --- |
| acquisition_failure | Allocation acquisition or initial ownership/publication failed |
| unhealthy_borrower | An unhealthy borrower or failed release publication prevents reuse |
| terminal_borrower_release | Healthy borrower releases without retaining the allocation |
| capacity_pressure | Admission owner retires an idle allocation to satisfy resource pressure |
| exclusive_admission | Admission owner retires idle allocations for exclusive work |
| invocation_cancellation | Invocation cancellation causes retirement |
| run_finalization | Normal run closure retires remaining ownership |

The lifecycle section SHALL allow at most 4,096 records, 4 MiB including its
metadata, and 65,536 bytes per record. Limits SHALL be authored instrumentation
policy inputs. Limit exhaustion SHALL disclose incomplete coverage, known
omission counts and bounded omitted identities. Repeated identical observations
SHALL be idempotent; conflicting allocation identities or terminal observations
SHALL mark diagnostic coverage partial and SHALL NOT overwrite accepted facts.
Readers SHALL reject contradictory published records. A failed retirement SHALL
remain unsettled; no observation can release physical ownership or capacity.
Optional observation, collection or publication failure SHALL NOT alter product
outcomes, failure precedence or cleanup authority. Records SHALL retain existing
privacy and safe-reference rules under REQ-844. Producers/readers/schema
projections SHALL migrate atomically, without legacy translation readers.

Rationale (non-normative): complete pages allow diagnosis of long paths without
unbounded output. Independent allocation coverage preserves lifecycle evidence
when detailed activity records reach their separate cap.

The `host-admission` view SHALL page the selected path's native admission
observations using the same TARGET, UNIT_ID, OFFSET, LIMIT and output bounds.
The default VIEW remains units. An independently bounded `host_admission` section
of execution diagnostics SHALL allow 16,384 records, 16 MiB including section
metadata, and the existing 65,536-byte record ceiling. It SHALL remain independent
of verbose execution and allocation-lifecycle truncation. Basic diagnostics
collect it; off diagnostics do not. Missing optional evidence is unavailable,
not an empty proof of no waiting. Limit exhaustion and conflicting records
SHALL disclose coverage and omissions; no oversized record may be truncated.

Each record SHALL bind a validated unit, opaque request identity when assigned,
and graph-monotonic clock. Native decisions SHALL expose queue position and mode,
requested active claims, effective capacities, charged residents and prospective additions,
current and persistent resource deficits, required ancestors, relevant holders,
and independent queue-priority/exclusive-fence blockers. Persistent deficits
retain required ancestor claims while removing independent active work. Decision
facts SHALL be captured by the same transaction/evaluator that grants or denies
admission, then published outside the admission mutex. Opaque diagnostic
references SHALL NOT disclose private lease capabilities or recovery paths.

Host-admission phases SHALL distinguish logical_slot, admission_transaction,
admission_wait, pressure_retirement and uncovered time. Repeated phase operations
MAY aggregate disjoint durations with explicit observation count and first/last
bounds; their span MUST NOT be reported as continuously occupied phase time.
Consecutive identical decisions for a request SHALL coalesce with first/last
observation bounds and count. They describe observations, not continuous evidence
between transactions. Simultaneous blockers SHALL NOT be summed as exclusive
wall-clock causes. Retirement observations SHALL record the owning trigger,
proposed resident references and settlement, without changing cleanup authority.
A retirement-evaluation observation SHALL bind the pending request, exact proposed
resident references, before/after persistent deficits, active referencing holders,
transaction outcome and capacity eligibility. Active references describe claim
ownership, not proof of an active logical borrower; borrower exclusion remains
the physical owner's separate required gate. The native counterfactual evaluator supplies
these facts; readers validate their declared consistency without independently
reconstructing weighted admission. Failed transactions establish no eligibility.
Execution index v5 and critical-path response v3 reference admission-record v2;
prior incompatible diagnostic shapes remain historical only.
Complete path totals and filtered totals remain independent of pagination.
The response SHALL label native disjoint phase totals as `host_phase_ms` and
canonical host phase totals as `host_admission_ms`. `host_uncovered_ms` SHALL sum,
per unit, the nonnegative difference between its canonical host phase and retained
native phase durations. Canonical event timestamps have one-millisecond rounding;
readers SHALL allow at most one millisecond per unit when reconciling native
submillisecond observations. Missing records SHALL remain uncovered. A record's
`requested_claims` describes the pending request; `active_holders` describes
admitted activity. Neither is a utilization measurement. Resident/prospective
references SHALL be disjoint within a decision. `request_ref` SHALL be null for
phase and retirement records because those operations can precede assignment or
span subordinate admission requests. Decision records SHALL bind the request's
opaque identity, stable sequence and mode. Their `outcome` SHALL distinguish a
committed admission transaction from a failed transaction; `granted` is true only
when the native transaction returns a successful grant. Diagnostic decisions
convey no independent ownership authority. Retirement reasons in this admission
section SHALL be `capacity_pressure`, `exclusive_admission`,
`terminal_borrower_release`, or `renderer_slot_pressure`; the last denotes a
logical renderer-slot constraint, not a host capacity deficit. Retirement records
SHALL include an explicit proposed resident set, including an empty set for a
logical-only slot, and `settled` or `unresolved` outcome. No failure detail or
private path is admitted into these public records.
Schemas, producers and readers SHALL migrate atomically without translation of
older retained evidence. Missing/truncated diagnostics cannot establish complete
attribution; malformed, unsafe or contradictory evidence is an artifact error.

Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-153.

### 10.10 Graph runtime and fixture ownership

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-852 — One graph execution owner.**
The Go graph runtime owns DAG scheduling, capacity and lock accounting, aging,
host admission, graph cache transactions, unit launch/wait/cancel, canonical events,
live status, required graph publication and finalization ordering. Existing graph
selection, scheduling, cache, failure precedence, timing, resource and cleanup
semantics MUST be preserved. Runtime tests exercise the owning policy through injected ports and independently
authored expected outcomes; a second scheduler implementation is not an oracle.
No JavaScript scheduler fallback or permanent runtime-selection switch is admitted.
Make remains the public entrypoint. The single installed `cartulary-harness`
binary has a thin composition root and cohesive reusable runtime, fixture,
admission, observation, session and secure-file libraries. Shared private-runtime
creation, borrowing, secret registration, recovery journals, stale cleanup and
retained scanning have one Go owner below graph, fixture and review coordination.
That owner MUST NOT depend on graph scheduling or fixture orchestration. Collection may remain an
isolated run-owned child of that binary for fault isolation and quietness; it
MUST NOT become a daemon or introduce an independent polling schedule. Read-only
status MUST NOT build, install or initialize writer state.
Workspace-descriptor inheritance and host-binding failures MUST retain a bounded
closed execution-stage/cause diagnostic alongside their existing normalized
failure. It MUST exclude raw errors, paths, tokens and process identities, and
MUST NOT replace the child exit or relax admission and cleanup boundaries.

Node owns source-aware compilation, graph modeling and selector validation, row
runners, runner-specific report adaptation and offline analysis. The compiler
MUST exit and be reaped before any graph unit launches; its catalog, source ASTs,
closures and caches MUST NOT remain in a resident graph coordinator. Node rows
continue validating their current selected inputs. Full public source preflight
MUST NOT be replaced by metadata-only fixture access.
Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-147

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-853 — Shared fixture coordination.**
One Go fixture implementation owns allocation, lease/reuse decisions, coordination,
recovery and ordered cleanup for graph and review callers. Graph and the Go review
coordinator call it directly. The Go review coordinator owns session admission,
registry authority, stopping, recovery serialization, cleanup ordering and terminal
transitions/publication. Browser actions, capture, analysis, report adaptation and
preparation recipes may remain in Node adapters, which report facts and normalized
outcomes rather than deciding session lifetimes. Existing service and browser lifecycle adapters
retain physical acquisition/reset/termination responsibilities. Owned resources
MUST drain before their dependencies close, borrowed resources MUST NOT be
terminated, partial acquisitions MUST retain recovery proof, repeated release and
close MUST be idempotent, and cleanup failures MUST preserve primary failure
precedence. Client loss MUST initiate owned cleanup; failed cleanup remains
explicit rather than inferring release from missing files or process names.

Physical process settlement has one reusable native owner. Process proof records
the actual process group and session identities rather than assuming that a group
leader is also a session leader. Signal delivery, leader exit and leader reaping
are not proof of descendant settlement. A trustworthy identity anchor must
authorize signaling; ambiguous or reused identities remain unresolved without
signaling unrelated processes. Release acknowledgement requires verified absence
of live owned members. The owner retains a direct child's identity anchor until
group settlement has completed where the launch/wait relationship permits it.

This settlement boundary applies to the source compiler, collector, physical
cleanup workers and browser-fixture supervisors as well as workload children.
Pipe closure and successful worker exit do not establish group settlement.
Compiler admission, resource release and finalization advancement MUST wait for
settlement or report an explicit unresolved cleanup failure. An optional
observation failure does not demote a required physical cleanup failure or
replace an earlier workload failure.

A diagnostic scope is private authority recorded before its producer can spawn.
The native owner resolves scope inspection and settlement against that exact
runtime/run/lease journal, validates UID, boot identity, start boundary and inherited
nonce, and rechecks process identity before signaling. Recovery after producer
death MUST work before daemon PID publication without surviving-parent authority.
A caller-supplied nonce or PID alone grants no authority. Inaccessible relevant
proof, incomplete discovery or conflicting identity MUST remain unresolved;
unrelated processes MUST NOT be signaled. Node adapters may consume bounded
inspection facts but MUST NOT implement a second discovery or signaling policy.

Temporary permission denial while reading relevant process proof MAY remain
pending within the same physical-settlement attempt and its existing deadline.
The native owner MUST reobserve complete scope membership and revalidate identity
before signaling; denied proof is neither absence nor authority. Persistent
denial MUST terminate as unresolved at that deadline. Reobservation MUST NOT
start another cleanup attempt, reset the deadline, or relax ownership checks.

An unanchored process-group observation MAY likewise remain pending within the
same bounded settlement attempt. Pending members MUST NOT be signaled or learned
as identity anchors. Complete discovery can establish group absence or restore a
previously trusted anchor for the existing owned-member settlement; the anchor
alone never establishes settlement. Persistent ambiguity
MUST fail closed with its process-group-anchor diagnostic; an unbounded caller
MUST reject ambiguity immediately. Reobservation does not create another cleanup
attempt, extend grace or establish the cause of an earlier failed invocation.

A failed process-handle acquisition MUST NOT establish settlement. If acquisition
reports an invalid argument for a previously observed member, a fresh process
lookup MAY establish that member's absence. The original complete-discovery loop
MUST still settle surviving members within its existing deadline. A live, reused
or unreadable process MUST retain the failure; the errno alone grants no absence
or signaling authority. Safe diagnostics distinguish handle acquisition,
identity revalidation and signal delivery.

Cleanup dependencies are explicit lifecycle edges, separate from files retained
as recovery authority. A failed resource blocks its dependencies, while proven
independent releases continue. Unknown edges remain unresolved. Each physical
service receives its own existing bounded cleanup attempt; independent services
may drain concurrently. Cleanup evidence distinguishes completed, failed and
blocked resources without replacing the primary failure.

The public `test-run-recover` maintenance command admits one exact retained graph
run using required Make-command-line inputs `RESULTS_DIR`, `RUNTIME_ROOT` and
`RUNTIME_LEASE_ID`. These identify the original result directory and private
runtime lease; no newest-run selection, path scan, PID inference or broad service
reset is permitted. The native owner MUST validate repository/run/lease bindings,
private-path protections and the original owner's death before external recovery.
It MUST reuse the shared cleanup evaluator and physical adapters, retain proof
when settlement fails, and leave original execution artifacts unchanged. Recovery
has separate tool-run evidence with redacted inputs and bounded resource-kind
outcome counts. Invalid identity fails before mutation with exit 2; unresolved
cleanup exits 12. A successful recovery does not convert the original failure
into a pass.

The same dependency evaluator governs ordinary close and explicit recovery for
all retained resource kinds, including diagnostic scopes, process proofs and
renderers. An edge names an exact resource identity in the same runtime/run/lease;
filesystem paths and recovery-file dependencies are not lifecycle identities.
Producers MUST declare edges or an explicit empty independence set before
acquiring a dependent resource. Missing or null edges mean unknown. Contradictory,
cyclic, foreign and unresolved references prevent successful cleanup; they MUST
NOT be interpreted as independence. Failed or blocked consumers protect their
transitive dependencies. Resources proven independent of those consumers still
receive their own existing bounded attempts. A repeated attempt joins the same
outcome; later explicit recovery starts a new attempt.

For example, a diagnostic scope consuming a browser declares that browser
resource as a dependency, and the browser declares its stack or suite dependency.
An unresolved diagnostic scope therefore retains that chain. A separate scope
with an explicit empty dependency set does not block an unrelated suite. A scope
whose declaration is missing cannot supply the same independence evidence.
Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-148

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-854 — Private preparation and lifecycle interfaces.**
The plan MUST carry `browser_lane_limit` resolved from topology-backed public
input. Planning and native renderer ownership use that same limit; mismatch with
the declared input fails closed. Renderer event slot IDs admit one through six.
Slots remain lazy, with existing compatibility, settlement, residency, pressure,
cleanup headroom and exclusive-measurement contracts. No independent planner or
pool default may override the topology. The dedicated UI-Review owner uses its
single dedicated renderer lifetime.

`cartulary.harness_runtime_plan.v6` carries the existing graph, projections,
provenance, capacity facts, validated launch bindings and cache inputs from the
source-aware compiler over an inherited private descriptor. It is limited to
33,554,432 bytes. The runtime MUST reject malformed/unknown versions, invalid
identities, graph/digest/reference closure failures, incomplete publication and
exhaustion before workload launch. No source object graph, callable behavior or
credentials may be retained as plan facts. The public surface MUST NOT accept
arbitrary executable plans or command strings. Runtime credentials remain under
existing private ownership and redaction boundaries.

The plan projects the task-surface owner's typed input forwarding into a bounded
private environment policy. Before unit dispatch, runtime clears all registered
target-local inputs and the enclosing Make input-source marker, then applies
only the selected command's admitted runtime forwarding. Selection and view
controls cannot leak into private children. Canonical unit arguments and owned
fixture-selection bindings remain separate. This policy is not retained in the
execution context and cannot carry credentials or become another input registry.

Private lifecycle interfaces carry only closed owner operations, bounded request
IDs, existing run/session/lease proof and closed outcomes. A frame is limited to
1,048,576 bytes; UI operation requests retain their separate 65,536-byte bound.
Session transport is private and
bound to the invoking owner; forged proof, unknown operations, duplicate settlement,
oversized/incomplete frames and late writes MUST fail closed. EOF or owner loss
initiates owned cleanup, with unresolved resources preserved for recovery.
A validated private transaction that fails MUST return a bounded, typed rejection
identifying the operation and failure category, without echoing credentials,
request values or arbitrary error strings. Transport failures remain distinct.
Process-proof diagnostics remain private and MUST NOT enter retained public
receipts. The native physical-process adapter and browser lifecycle adapters MUST
preserve a closed cleanup diagnostic on failed settlement. The shared
`cartulary.harness_cleanup_diagnostic.v4` attachment contains only schema identity,
closed stage and cause categories, a bounded errno and optional closed identity
boundary/opaque producer-registration reference; its transport is limited to
4,096 bytes. It excludes process identities, proof paths, credentials and
arbitrary exception strings. Adapters validate it before forwarding; malformed,
oversized or missing diagnostics cannot turn a failed cleanup into success.
Native fixture diagnostics MUST distinguish resource-inventory/graph validation,
physical-command settlement, exact resource release, resident-capacity release,
fixture publication and host-release boundaries. A more specific validated nested
process/browser diagnosis takes precedence over a caller's boundary label.
An acknowledgement failure remains distinguishable from physical settlement.
Recovery preservation distinguishes required-proof validation from disposable-file
purge; an absent required proof remains an unresolved failure.
The native run's terminal diagnostic may project this safe detail without changing
primary/secondary failure classification or granting cleanup authority. Rejection reporting MUST NOT turn incomplete authority into success.
No lifecycle interface is a public general-purpose command runner. Superseded
fixture-session transport MUST be removed after callers use direct Go coordination;
old live sessions drain with their running version, without a legacy recovery
reader or historical receipt rewrite. Typed schemas and
machine projections, not Markdown or a second authored validator registry, define
its executable shape. Native and Node schema acceptance MUST agree on shared
fixtures, including duplicate keys and prototype-like members.
Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-147–148

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-855 — Single-owner completion boundaries.**
Graph execution, shared sessions and fixture coordination MUST each have one active policy
owner across their callers. Superseded runtime/broker policy, alternate dispatch,
and compatibility forwarding interfaces MUST NOT remain active. Required graph
publication precedes ordinary diagnostic drain; retained scanning begins only
after ordinary producers stop. The sole subsequent retained write remains
REQ-847's bounded receipt. Clock placement, container proof, observation cadence,
uncertainty, size/deadline limits and retained-format acceptance sets are unchanged.
Historical failures MUST NOT be relabelled, and diagnostics remain default-off.
Functional completion does not establish any harness performance claim. Implementation sequencing and rollback
transactions belong to the human tracker, not executable conformance inputs.
Shared scanning does not merge graph and UI publication protocols: UI review
retains REQ-502/616's terminal-publication and retained-boundary scan ordering.
Standalone tools, smoke execution, frontend artifact producers and local-service
adapters use the shared native private-runtime owner; borrowing never grants root
deletion authority. Persistent service proof survives short-lived commands without
a new resident supervisor. Tests use independently specified expected outcomes;
a retired JavaScript implementation MUST NOT remain a native test oracle.

Runtime creation binds the canonical repository and retained run root in private
owner proof. Borrowing and recovery MUST validate those creation bindings; supplied
paths alone never confer authority. Distinct physical lifecycle output roots are
explicit owner-bound destinations, not a general arbitrary-root exception. Private
wire operations without current production consumers MUST be removed; necessary
native methods and their behavioral tests do not require wire exposure.

Native runtime creation MUST perform bounded stale-root maintenance within the
selected scratch root. Age alone never grants deletion authority: an eligible
root is at least 24 hours old, has valid private ownership proof and a proven-dead
original process, and has no unresolved resource records or sealed finalization
authority. An absent or validated empty recovery journal proves resource settlement
only; mere directory presence MUST NOT prevent reclamation of an unsealed root.
A sealed root can still own unresolved terminal publication or retained-scan
authority after its resources drain and MUST remain available for exact recovery. Busy roots and live or uncertain owners remain untouched. Cleanup
MUST fence and settle admitted detail producers and recovery attempts before
removing a root. Enumeration is bounded to 8192 entries and physical removals to
64 per acquisition; retained entries MUST NOT consume the removal budget or
permanently hide later eligible roots. Invalid ownership or resource records fail
closed. Ordinary terminal cleanup remains immediate; unresolved resources retain
exact recovery proof. No name/age-only sweep of other scratch, retained evidence
or machine caches is permitted. A root-location change MUST NOT relocate live
allocations or rewrite historical recovery paths.

Shared retained scanning MUST recognize the existing secret syntax independently
of input fragmentation, key/value length and intervening whitespace. Use bounded
streaming state without full-file buffering or silent size cutoffs. Registered
secret matching, redaction exclusions, filesystem safety and the existing policy
identity remain unchanged.
Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-147–149


## 11. Service and Fixture Lifecycle

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-400**
Service-backed targets MUST run in exactly one service mode: `owned` or `attach`.
Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-007

| Mode     | Selection rule                                      | Missing variables                                                      | Ownership                                                                     |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `owned`  | `CARTULARY_TEST_SERVICES_MODE=owned` or omitted.    | Not applicable.                                                        | Harness starts and cleans suite resources.                                    |
| `attach` | `CARTULARY_TEST_SERVICES_MODE=attach`.              | Any missing or invalid session descriptor fails with `configuration_error`. | Harness borrows descriptor-proven containers and deletes only run-owned resources. |

### Interactive browser design review

`browser-design-review` is a helper-only interactive preparation command. It
MUST remain outside default verification sets and MUST NOT emit passing product
catalog rows. Its private lifecycle smoke assertion remains reachable through
owner selection and `harness-contract SUITE=lifecycle`. `REVIEW_PROFILE` is an
optional Make-command-line, environment, or default input with exactly `default`
and `network_flow_claimed` as values; omission selects `network_flow_claimed`.
Empty or unknown values fail as `usage_error` with exit `2` before preparation.
The input is forwarded only as runtime environment, with its value available in
session diagnostics. Machine output mode is unsupported as for `dev`.

Each invocation MUST own a fresh suite runtime, service-broker browser lease,
private database/object namespace, and sealed frontend artifact. Preparation MUST
validate the current v7 attachment before API seeding or browser use. The ordinary
browser lifecycle adapter retains exclusive ownership of startup and teardown;
these commands MUST NOT attach development services or bypass process, source,
profile, or build identity checks. Synthetic seed inputs MUST come from machine
contracts and fixture assets outside Markdown. Credentials and authenticator
material MUST remain in the private runtime and MUST be removed on completion.

The interactive command remains alive until interruption or owned-runtime failure.
The smoke command closes after preparation and browser observations. Acquisition,
preparation, and observation failures MUST stop dependent work. Both commands MUST
attempt owned browser, service, and private-runtime cleanup, retaining the primary
failure when cleanup also fails. Startup, lease, cleanup and secret-scan evidence
remain retained. A review source descriptor may occupy `run-manifest.json` for
lifecycle source binding, but MUST be labelled `interactive_design_review`, MUST
NOT claim the canonical harness-run schema, and MUST NOT manufacture graph, row,
conformance, or release success. Review screenshots are diagnostic observations;
ordinary review MUST NOT alter committed goldens.

### 11.0 Postgres Fixture Model

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-405**
Transaction fixtures MUST settle rollback and connection close with independent
five-second client-operation budgets detached from test cancellation. Reuse
requires both operations to succeed. Any uncertainty MUST invalidate the package
fixture before its mutex is released; later borrowers fail before accessing it.
Cleanup failures MUST produce typed cleanup evidence without replacing an
existing product failure. Database ownership records remain available to final
cleanup. The failed product test MUST NOT be retried.

Fixture selection MUST be intent-based so catalog growth does not turn setup
into hidden critical-path cost. The catalog's explicit `fixture_capability` is
the sole row-level isolation request. Helper code MUST fail closed when its
requested capability differs from the selected row or when no active broker can
satisfy it.
Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-007, TH-HARNESS-AC-018

| Capability | Intended use | Required isolation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `none` | Pure work with no managed fixture. | No broker resource. |
| `postgres_transaction` | Store work whose writes can be fully rolled back. | One transaction; committed-state observation is rejected. |
| `postgres_dedicated` | Committed state, DB identity, process, recovery, or isolation-sensitive work. | One clean database leased to each test owner; compatible rows may share only the Go process. |
| `postgres_migration` | Upgrade, downgrade, replay, boundary, or backfill paths. | One fresh database per test owner and retained full-chain proof. |
| `object_store_namespace` | Isolated object-store effects. | Unique test-owned namespace unless the explicit package-reuse helper owns the scope. |
| `managed_process` | Process lifecycle or binary evidence. | Owned process group and unique ports. |
| `browser_stack` | Browser groups and their application stack. | Broker-owned DB, namespace, processes, and port set. |

The migrated Postgres template key is derived from sorted migration inputs and
the migration-runner identity. Lease events and summaries MUST include schema
digest, capability, ownership, and compatibility key where applicable. Attach
mode MUST fail before child execution when the advertised schema digest does
not match local migration inputs.

Transaction leases MUST prove rollback and reject work that uses a connection
outside the rollback transaction or requires committed cross-connection
visibility. A transaction row MUST be explicitly admitted by the typed
PostgreSQL fixture policy registry; registry omission fails catalog validation.
Dedicated and migration leases MUST be unique to one test owner. Compatible
exact-symbol rows MAY share a Go process, but MUST NOT share the database,
database handle, eager finalizer, or cleanup record. Rows
involving process lifecycle, recovery, schema mutation, DDL,
advisory locks, database identity, background work, WebSocket observers, or any
unproven cleanup surface MUST use dedicated isolation rather than transaction
scope. The registry validator MUST close every active PostgreSQL row
from the current catalog and reject stale or surplus shared-scope approvals.

A graph-owned suite MUST acquire only the union of its selected units’ declared
service dependencies, and its lease MUST identify only acquired resources.
Standalone full-suite commands explicitly own the complete service scope.
Lifecycle acceptance examples MUST include a pure selection that starts no
managed services, a PostgreSQL-only selection, and distinct consumers sharing
one suite owner while retaining their declared isolation. Nested wrapper counts,
an unconditional service pair, or the absence of per-test database drops do not
establish this contract. Installed boundary evidence MUST confirm successful
owned cleanup and that detaching a borrower leaves its service owner usable;
missing required infrastructure is a setup failure, not a passing skip.

Performance-fixture builders MUST use an explicit builder policy owned by the
performance-fixture profile. The current builder profile claims bounded CPU,
memory, I/O, and process resources plus one PostgreSQL lane. It MUST NOT inherit
the browser consumer profile and MUST NOT claim a browser stack, port lane, or
object-store lane merely because the resulting fixture is later consumed by a
browser measurement.

The broker creates clean dedicated databases on demand from the current sealed
template; asynchronous replenishment and a writable clone pool are unsupported.
Failed reset, health, cleanup, or contamination validation quarantines the lease
and replaces it; a quarantined lease is never readmitted for reuse. Cleanup is
idempotent and records whether each resource was returned, destroyed, borrowed,
or already absent. Cancellation and partial startup follow the same ownership
rules. No capacity increase may substitute for assigning the least expensive
capability that still proves the row's isolation contract.

Every per-test dedicated or migration database MUST be deleted eagerly after
its owning application runtime, background work, pool, and handle have closed.
After exact ownership is proved, cleanup MUST issue at most one atomic
`DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS ... WITH (FORCE)`. There is no ordinary preflight,
retry after timeout, or split terminate-then-drop path. Force terminates remaining
connections; it does not bypass PostgreSQL checkpoint synchronization and MUST
NOT conceal an earlier owner shutdown failure. Invalid ownership, rejected
admission or pre-cancellation permits no destructive statement.

Every cooperating harness-owned create, clone, template state mutation and drop
MUST acquire a target-specific exclusive session-advisory lock on the same
physical PostgreSQL connection that executes the mutation. A separate lock-holder
MUST NOT release exclusion while a cancelled backend can still execute. Retired
connections retain server-side exclusion until settlement; unrelated targets
remain independent. PostgreSQL lock wait ordering supplies admission; polling,
try-lock loops, service-global quiescence and hash-derived stripes are forbidden.
Global concurrency belongs exclusively to typed graph resource claims.

The common cleanup owner SHALL establish one deadline after validating inputs
and before target admission. Its deadline SHALL be the earlier of the supplied
parent deadline, when present, and 35 seconds after establishing the cleanup
context. A parent without a deadline SHALL receive the same 35-second default;
a longer parent SHALL NOT extend it. The deadline SHALL remain unchanged through
admission, the one drop and settlement. A phase transition SHALL NOT restart or
replenish the cleanup budget.

| Cleanup boundary | Effective allowance | Required behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Target admission | The lesser of 15 seconds and remaining owner time | Acquire the target lock on the mutation connection; expiry or cancellation permits no destructive statement. |
| One forced drop | Remaining owner time after admission | Execute at most one owned atomic drop; no independent 20-second cutoff, retry, replacement connection or checkpoint bypass. |
| Lock release | The lesser of 2 seconds and remaining owner time | Cancellation may be detached solely to attempt settlement; the owner's deadline remains authoritative. A retired connection does not authorize reuse of uncertain resources. |
| Connection close and physical settlement | Existing owner-finalization contract | Preserve failures and cleanup authority; deadline expiry or a returned client call does not prove server-side settlement. |

Effective admission and operation budgets SHALL be reported separately from
elapsed durations. The shared cleanup-observation contract SHALL use version 3,
with `operation_budget_ms` in `0..35000`; the admission bound remains
`0..15000`. Unadmitted operations SHALL retain zero operation duration and budget.
The old version-2 component SHALL be removed from current schema attachments;
all references and generated validators SHALL migrate atomically. No translation
reader or compatibility setting SHALL be introduced. Retained records remain
bound to their actual source and contract epoch.

Failed acquisition receives fresh bounded cleanup independent of cancelled setup,
but acquired resources MUST NOT escape their owning cleanup lifetime through an
unbounded background context. Timeout means uncertain cleanup, not proof that
the server stopped or the resource disappeared. Operation, admission, unlock,
connection-close and prior owner-close failures SHALL remain independently
attributable. Failed eager cleanup SHALL retain its original failure even if later
service retirement completes. Scheduler claims, isolation and admission ordering
remain unchanged.

Acceptance under TH-HARNESS-AC-007 SHALL prove absent, longer, shorter, expired
and cancelled parent contexts; one unchanged owner deadline across admission and
drop; operation use of remaining owner time rather than a reset allowance;
pre-operation cancellation with no statement; exactly one drop on success or
failure; preserved operation/unlock/close causes; and native/schema rejection of
negative, oversized or unadmitted operation budgets. Live fixtures SHALL cover
idempotent owned deletion, active connections, same-target exclusion, unrelated
target progress, delayed barrier observations and the affected eager finalizers.

Rationale (non-normative): admission and execution compete for one finite cleanup
lifetime. A separate operation cap discarded unused admission time even when a
checkpoint could settle within that existing lifetime. Sharing the deadline
removes that unnecessary cutoff without extending the owner's overall allowance
or changing database durability.

Recovery browser cleanup MUST stop both owned HTTP/runtime/background chains,
close pools/handles, then delete the two independent owned databases concurrently
with at most two operations and matching resource claims. Partial acquisition
uses the same ownership discipline. The existing 35-second parent graceful
allowance includes at most 30 seconds of child cleanup work and 5 seconds of
settlement/reporting reserve. The allowance is passed through the existing launch
contract rather than duplicated across Go and JavaScript. Database lifecycle
records report effective deadlines. Process-stop backstops retain uncertain
ownership; abandoned work or a later janitor success cannot rewrite the original
cleanup outcome or prematurely release capacity.

A failed or
interrupted eager cleanup remains in the private
resource ledger for suite teardown or stale recovery; those mechanisms are
idempotent fallbacks and MUST NOT be the successful hot path. Successful
per-test databases MUST NOT emit retained-resource events or appear in an
exhaustive retained summary list. Per-test object-store buckets and prefixes
follow the same owner-finalization rule. Explicit object-store package reuse
remains package-scoped and is cleaned or reset only at its declared package or
suite boundary. A browser session namespace remains stable across stateful
generations: reset MUST empty the exact owned bucket in place and prove its
put/head/delete mutation path before the next generation is admitted. Reset
MUST NOT delete and recreate that namespace. Successful session finalization
deletes the namespace; failed reset or finalization remains recoverable through
the private ledger.

### 11.1 Lifecycle Machine Contract

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-403**
A lifecycle machine is normative only when this NLSpec explicitly labels it normative. A representational lifecycle diagram MUST be labeled non-normative, MUST cite its owning requirements, and MUST NOT add behavior. A normative harness lifecycle machine MUST define scope, instance key, closed state set, closed event set, terminal states, transition table, guard precedence, failure mapping, authoritative state derivation, observable evidence, and conformance criteria. Illegal transitions MUST NOT mutate state, MUST fail closed with Section 9 failure classification, and MUST emit retained evidence. State-advancing artifact writes MUST be atomic and idempotent, or the machine MUST define guardrails that prevent unsafe re-execution. Parent lifecycle logic MUST depend only on child terminal status and retained artifacts, not on child in-memory state.
Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-017

Implementations MAY realize a normative lifecycle machine with ordinary control flow, tables, generated code, or a state-machine library. The runtime mechanism is not normative. The closed states, events, transitions, failure mapping, and observable evidence are normative.

Normative lifecycle-machine state and event names MUST be ASCII `lower_snake_case`. A transition table is closed by default: any `(state, event)` pair not listed by the owning machine is illegal.

### 11.2 Normative Service Suite Lifecycle Machine

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-404**
The service suite lifecycle machine is normative for every service-backed suite in `owned` or `attach` mode. The machine ID is `test_services_suite_lifecycle_v1`. The machine instance key is `suite_id`. The authoritative transition record is `_shared/test-services/<suite-id>/lifecycle-events.jsonl`, where every line MUST validate as `cartulary.test_services.lifecycle.v3`. The current state is `requested` before the first lifecycle event and otherwise the `to_state` of the last valid lifecycle event. A missing, malformed, non-sequential, or transition-invalid lifecycle event stream after a suite directory or lease exists MUST fail closed with `failure_class=artifact` and `failure_reason=artifact_error`. The service lease remains cleanup-proof evidence and MUST NOT be interpreted as a transition log.
Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-007, TH-HARNESS-AC-017

Lifecycle event `seq` starts at `1`, increments by `1`, and has no gaps. Events MUST be processed in emitted sequence order. When competing conditions are observed before the next event is emitted, guard precedence is:

| State           | Precedence rule                                      |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `starting`      | `startup_failed` before `readiness_passed`.          |
| `running_child` | `interrupt_received` before `child_started` before `child_finished` when multiple child signals are observed before the next event is emitted. |
| `cleaning`      | `cleanup_failed` before `cleanup_succeeded`.         |
| all others      | The transition table has at most one allowed event.  |

#### States

| State           | Kind         | Invariants                                                                 | Observable signals                                                                 |
| --------------- | ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `requested`     | initial      | Suite setup has been requested but no lifecycle event has been emitted.    | No lifecycle event stream exists for the selected `suite_id`.                      |
| `starting`      | intermediate | Suite setup or attach-mode validation is in progress; child work has not started. | Latest lifecycle event has `to_state=starting`; lease or startup diagnostics exist when the suite writes them. |
| `ready`         | intermediate | Required services or supplied attach endpoints have passed readiness.      | Latest lifecycle event has `to_state=ready`; readiness diagnostics are retained when produced. |
| `running_child` | intermediate | One or more child work units are executing under the suite.                 | Latest lifecycle event has `to_state=running_child`; the event references child logs or target artifacts when known and reports `active_child_count`. |
| `interrupted`   | intermediate | Cancellation or interruption was observed while child work was active.     | Latest lifecycle event has `to_state=interrupted` and `failure_reason=cancelled_or_interrupted`. |
| `cleaning`      | intermediate | Owned teardown or attach-mode diagnostic finalization is in progress.      | Latest lifecycle event has `to_state=cleaning`; lease `cleanup_state=in_progress` when a lease exists. |
| `cleaned`       | terminal     | Required cleanup or attach-mode finalization completed.                   | Latest lifecycle event has `to_state=cleaned`; lease `cleanup_state=completed` or `deferred`. |
| `failed_start`  | terminal     | Startup, attach validation, preflight, or readiness failed before child work started. | Latest lifecycle event has `to_state=failed_start`; failure summary records the Section 9 reason. |
| `cleanup_failed` | terminal   | Cleanup or finalization failed and retained proof remains for investigation or stale janitor handling. | Latest lifecycle event has `to_state=cleanup_failed`; lease `cleanup_state=failed` when a lease exists. |

#### Events

| Event                | Definition                                                                 |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `start_services`     | Begin owned suite startup or attach-mode suite validation.                 |
| `readiness_passed`   | All readiness predicates required by Section 11.4 passed before deadline.  |
| `startup_failed`     | Startup, attach validation, preflight, fixture preparation, or readiness failed before child work started. |
| `child_started`      | A child target, child command, or scheduler work unit started under a ready suite. |
| `child_finished`     | An active child target, child command, or scheduler work unit exited and its status was recorded. |
| `interrupt_received` | The wrapper observed cancellation or process interruption while child work was active. |
| `cleanup_started`    | Teardown, cleanup, or attach-mode diagnostic finalization started.         |
| `cleanup_succeeded`  | Teardown, cleanup, or attach-mode diagnostic finalization completed.       |
| `cleanup_failed`     | Teardown, cleanup, or attach-mode diagnostic finalization failed.          |

#### Transition Rules

| From state      | Event                | Guard                                      | To state         | Required actions                                                              | Failure mapping                                                                 | Observable evidence |
| --------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- |
| `requested`     | `start_services`     | Configuration resolved; `suite_id` allocated; no prior lifecycle event exists. | `starting`       | Create suite directory as needed; write initial lease or attach diagnostic when applicable; append lifecycle event. | If setup cannot begin, fail before mutation with `configuration_error`, `preflight_error`, or `fixture_error` according to the failed predicate. | Lifecycle event `seq=1`; lease or diagnostic artifact refs when present. |
| `starting`      | `readiness_passed`   | All required readiness predicates passed.  | `ready`          | Append lifecycle event and retain readiness diagnostics when produced.         | none                                                                            | Lifecycle event with readiness artifact refs. |
| `starting`      | `startup_failed`     | Any startup, attach validation, preflight, fixture, or readiness predicate failed before child start. | `failed_start`   | Append lifecycle event; record failure summary; terminate known partial resources or leave proof for stale janitor. | `preflight_error`, `service_start_error`, `service_readiness_timeout`, `fixture_error`, or `configuration_error` according to Sections 9 and 11.4. | Lifecycle event with failure fields and proof artifact refs. |
| `ready`         | `child_started`      | Child key is non-empty and not already active. | `running_child`  | Append lifecycle event; set `active_child_count=1`; retain child log or target artifact refs when known. | Child start failure before process launch is `child_target_failure` or `fixture_error` according to the wrapper boundary. | Lifecycle event with child key, `active_child_count=1`, and child artifact refs when known. |
| `running_child` | `child_started`      | Child key is non-empty and not already active. | `running_child`  | Append lifecycle event; increment `active_child_count`; retain child log or target artifact refs when known. | Duplicate or missing child key is an illegal transition. | Lifecycle event with child key and incremented `active_child_count`. |
| `running_child` | `child_finished`     | Active child key is known, child status has been recorded, at least two children remain active before this event, and no interruption wins by guard precedence. | `running_child` | Append lifecycle event; decrement `active_child_count`; retain child status and artifacts. | Unknown child key or negative active count is an illegal transition. Child failure is recorded for primary failure selection by Section 9.1; the lifecycle state itself is not terminal. | Lifecycle event with child key, child status artifact refs, and decremented `active_child_count`. |
| `running_child` | `child_finished`     | Active child key is known, child status has been recorded, exactly one child remains active before this event, and no interruption wins by guard precedence. | `ready` | Append lifecycle event; set `active_child_count=0`; retain child status and artifacts. | Unknown child key or negative active count is an illegal transition. Child failure is recorded for primary failure selection by Section 9.1; the lifecycle state itself is not terminal. | Lifecycle event with child key, child status artifact refs, and `active_child_count=0`. |
| `running_child` | `interrupt_received` | Cancellation or signal wins by guard precedence. | `interrupted`    | Append lifecycle event and preserve child/interruption diagnostics when available; report current `active_child_count`. | `failure_class=interrupted`, `failure_reason=cancelled_or_interrupted`.         | Lifecycle event with interruption fields and `active_child_count`. |
| `ready`         | `cleanup_started`    | No child is running and cleanup/finalization is required. | `cleaning`       | Set lease `cleanup_state=in_progress` when a lease exists; append lifecycle event. | Cleanup start failure is recorded as `cleanup_error` without deleting unproven resources. | Lifecycle event and updated lease. |
| `interrupted`   | `cleanup_started`    | Interruption has been recorded and cleanup/finalization is required. | `cleaning`       | Set lease `cleanup_state=in_progress` when a lease exists; append lifecycle event. | Primary interruption failure is preserved by Section 9.1.                       | Lifecycle event and updated lease. |
| `cleaning`      | `cleanup_succeeded`  | Required cleanup or finalization completed. | `cleaned`        | Set lease `cleanup_state=completed` or `deferred`; append lifecycle event.     | Success unless an earlier primary failure exists.                               | Lifecycle event and final lease. |
| `cleaning`      | `cleanup_failed`     | Cleanup or finalization failed.            | `cleanup_failed` | Set lease `cleanup_state=failed`; append lifecycle event; retain proof for stale janitor. | `cleanup_error`; Section 9.1 decides whether it becomes the public exit-code driver. | Lifecycle event, final lease, and cleanup diagnostics. |

Any listed event presented in an unlisted state MUST append a lifecycle event with `transition_status=illegal`, `from_state` equal to `to_state`, `failure_class=harness`, and `failure_reason=scheduler_accounting_error`, then fail without mutating suite state. An unrecognized event token MUST be rejected before lifecycle mutation and MUST NOT be appended to the schema-valid lifecycle event stream. A terminal state MUST reject every later event as illegal.

Lifecycle failure events MUST carry normalized Section 9 failure fields. `startup_failed`, `interrupt_received`, `cleanup_failed`, and illegal-transition lifecycle events MUST set non-null `failure_class` and `failure_reason` in the lifecycle stream. Non-failure lifecycle events MUST preserve `failure_class=null` and `failure_reason=null` unless a later schema revision adds a narrower event-specific diagnostic field.

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-406**
The service-suite lifecycle active-child counter is normative. `child_started`, `child_finished`, and `interrupt_received` lifecycle events MUST include `active_child_count`. `ready + child_started` sets the count to `1`; `running_child + child_started` increments it; `running_child + child_finished` decrements it and remains in `running_child` while the count is greater than `0`; `running_child + child_finished` transitions to `ready` when the count becomes `0`. Negative active counts, missing child identity, duplicate `child_started` for the same active child key, and `child_finished` for an unknown active child key are illegal transitions under Section 11.2.
Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-017, TH-HARNESS-AC-033

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-411**
Every current-run service suite MUST retain `_shared/test-services/<suite-id>/service-scope.json` as `cartulary.test_services.scope.v2` after the suite artifact directory exists and before scheduler classification consumes service diagnostics. The summary MUST contain suite identity, target, readiness generation, preflight, cleanup, started-service and fixture aggregate counts, complete failure counts by normalized class and reason, no more than ten deterministic normalized exemplars per failure class, and the ten slowest fixture activities. Fixture totals and the distinct strategy-aggregate count MUST remain exact. A strategy aggregate is identified by the exact ASCII tuple of service, target, operation, preparation strategy, fixture policy, fixture class, and reuse scope; caller-package and test identities are separate hotspot and slowest-event dimensions and MUST NOT change strategy-aggregate identity. The retained strategy diagnostic contains at most 32 aggregates, selected by descending total duration, then descending event count, then that ASCII aggregate identity. It MUST NOT retain exhaustive database, bucket, package, or test-name inventories. When a service suite fails, `failure` MUST include normalized non-null `failure_class` and `failure_reason` fields. Startup preflight failures map to `infra/preflight_error`; service startup failures map to `infra/service_start_error`; readiness deadline failures map to `infra/service_readiness_timeout`; fixture preparation failures map to `harness/fixture_error` unless Section 9 assigns `artifact_error`; cleanup failures map to `harness/cleanup_error`.

Each producer MUST append bounded `cartulary.test_services.journal_event.v2`
records to one owner-only producer journal. Producer identity is stable for the
process and `seq` starts at one and increases without gaps. Collation sorts by
event time, producer identity, and sequence. A reader MAY ignore only an
incomplete trailing crash record; it MUST reject a malformed completed record,
duplicate sequence, or gap. Every scope refresh MUST write and sync an
owner-only sibling, atomically replace the prior summary, and sync the
containing directory, so readers observe one complete old or new document.

Exact owned-resource state belongs only in a mode-`0600`
`cartulary.test_services.resource_ledger.v2`. Cleanup and stale recovery MUST
validate ownership proof from that ledger before mutation. Successful cleanup
deletes the ledger. Cleanup failure MAY retain only a redacted contained copy
needed for recovery. Browser admission MUST consume a compact
`cartulary.test_services.browser_admission.v2` proof and MUST NOT copy the scope
summary; the proof closes suite/session identity, readiness generation,
required services, container proof, source digest, and the admitted scope
digest.

Every executable browser cohort MUST acquire and hold its browser-stack lease
while it consumes admission, prepares clean state and executes. The graph MUST
NOT interpose a commandless readiness or separately admitted reset unit that
releases the allocation before that consumer starts. Later compatible cohorts
may borrow the same healthy allocation after their own preparation; the terminal
consumer releases it. Successful browser-session startup MUST bind backend and frontend
readiness in the top-level lifecycle, atomically publish both the immutable
stack and compact admission, and verify that both are owner-only regular files
before returning the allocation. Missing readiness identity or either missing
publication is a startup failure; publication MUST NOT return success with a
partial evidence set. Every admission, lease, stack, and final verification
command MUST propagate failure explicitly even when timing instrumentation has
disabled shell fail-fast behavior. A browser-session artifact directory is a
single-use identity: startup MUST reject a pre-existing directory and MUST NOT
clear, replace, or retry publication under that identity.

Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-007, TH-HARNESS-AC-014, TH-HARNESS-AC-017, TH-HARNESS-AC-025

**TH-HARNESS-REQ-410**
An authoritative service-backed Go row MUST make its fixture capability and
complete service dependency set explicit in the catalog and at the helper call
site. The scheduler MUST pass the canonical sorted set through
`CARTULARY_HARNESS_SERVICE_DEPENDENCIES`. Before `appsupport`, `pgtest`, or
`s3test` attaches to or creates any resource, a shared acquisition guard MUST
prove every helper-required service is assigned to the work unit. A missing,
unknown, duplicate, unsorted, or runtime-incompatible declaration fails as
`harness/fixture_error` before either service is touched. A generic helper MUST
NOT silently fall back to a dedicated database, transaction,
migration database, object-store namespace, managed process, browser stack, or
implicit scheduler claim.

A direct developer `go test` invocation is noncanonical. When the assignment
environment variable is absent, it MAY proceed only because the helper call
supplies its explicit required-service list; this does not synthesize a graph
claim, canonical evidence, or compatibility fallback. Non-row
implementation-support tests follow the same explicit call-site rule.

Verified by: TH-HARNESS-AC-007, TH-HARNESS-AC-056

### 11.3 Lease Fields

Lease files MUST be written before child work starts, MUST be redacted before retention, and MUST be written atomically as a complete JSON file. A lease is evidence for cleanup only when its resource proof matches the actual resource state; cleanup MUST verify labels, prefixes, generated names, or equivalent proof and MUST NOT trust the lease path alone.

| Field              | Type                                                               |                        Required |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------: |
| `schema_id`        | string, `cartulary.test_services.lease.v3`                         |                             yes |
| `lease_id`         | non-empty opaque lease identifier                                  |                             yes |
| `suite_id`         | 24 lowercase hex chars                                             |                             yes |
| `target`           | string                                                             |                             yes |
| `mode`             | `owned` or `attach`                                                |                             yes |
| `ownership_mode`   | `owned` or `attach`                                                |                             yes |
| `result_root`      | normalized path                                                    |                             yes |
| `run_id`           | normalized run ID                                                  |                             yes |
| `run_root`         | normalized run-root path                                           |                             yes |
| `owner_pid`        | integer process ID for the owning wrapper                          |                             yes |
| `created_at`       | RFC3339 UTC                                                        |                             yes |
| `heartbeat_at`     | RFC3339 UTC                                                        |                              no |
| `expires_at`       | RFC3339 UTC                                                        |                              no |
| `resources[]`      | redacted resource records with service kind, logical ID, and proof | yes in owned mode, may be empty |
| `proof_labels`     | object of required labels used to prove container ownership        |           yes for container use |
| `proof_prefixes`   | object of generated DB/bucket/path prefixes used to prove ownership | yes for DB, bucket, or path use |
| `cleanup_state`    | `not_started`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `failed`, or `deferred` |                             yes |

### 11.4 Readiness Deadlines

Owned PostgreSQL acquisition SHALL distinguish container startup, mapped-endpoint
resolution, SQL readiness, security/capability validation, generation initialization
and ready-binding publication. The startup owner SHALL impose an outer cap of
180 seconds and one deadline of at most 35 seconds per attempt. Every owned
acquisition entry point, including direct helper callers, SHALL impose these caps.
The PostgreSQL acquisition owner SHALL own the attempt cap; suite composition
SHALL NOT supply a separate attempt-timeout option. Callers MAY supply an earlier
context deadline, which SHALL bound both caps. A nil acquisition context SHALL
fail before provider preflight or acquisition. Endpoint resolution SHALL have a 15-second cap within
that attempt. After endpoint resolution, SQL readiness SHALL consume the remaining
attempt budget; it SHALL NOT start an independent readiness window or extend the
attempt deadline. Polling SHALL use a 250 ms interval. Each SQL probe, including
its security/capability checks, SHALL have a cap of 5 seconds bounded by the
remaining attempt deadline. Admission waiting SHALL NOT consume these allowances.

The readiness operation SHALL require a non-nil context with a finite parent
deadline. It SHALL reject a missing or unbounded parent before launching any
probe. An already cancelled or expired parent SHALL retain that cancellation or
expiry outcome, with zero probes, including when the cancelled parent has no
deadline. This interface SHALL NOT supply an implicit replacement timeout.
Authentication, security-policy and required-capability rejection SHALL remain
terminal. Entering SQL readiness SHALL exclude a replacement startup attempt.
Generation initialization and template migration are distinct from connectivity;
the owner SHALL publish a ready binding only after its required prerequisites
succeed.

**Rationale — non-normative:** A published Docker port can precede completion of
PostgreSQL bootstrap. One attempt-owned readiness budget avoids a second deadline
that begins before SQL can become ready, while preserving the total startup cap.

PostgreSQL startup failures MUST retain bounded normalized phase, probe counts,
configured and effective budgets, limiting deadline, elapsed time and cleanup
outcome through the existing service-scope diagnostic extension boundary.
The v6 diagnostic SHALL omit the retired `sql_window_ms` field. For each phase,
`configured_ms` SHALL denote an independent phase cap; zero SHALL mean no such
cap. `effective_ms` SHALL record the available budget at phase entry, clamped to
zero for an already expired parent. `limiting_deadline` SHALL identify the
boundary supplying that budget. The following mapping SHALL apply:

| Phase | `configured_ms` | Effective budget and limiting boundary |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `container_start` | `0` | Remaining attempt budget; `parent` |
| `endpoint_resolution` | `15000` | Minimum of phase cap and remaining attempt budget; `phase` unless the parent is earlier |
| `sql_connectivity` | `0` | Remaining attempt budget; `parent` |
| `security_capability` | `5000` | Remaining current probe budget, bounded by the attempt; `parent` when earlier than the phase cap |
| `generation_initialization` | `0` | Remaining attempt budget; `parent` |

A SQL-readiness phase claiming a nonzero independent cap or a non-parent limiting
boundary SHALL be rejected as contradictory evidence. The schema, producer and
all current consumers SHALL migrate atomically; no v4 translation reader or
compatibility fallback SHALL be introduced.

Transport text, endpoints, credentials and raw provider errors MUST NOT enter
that diagnostic. A failed allocation MUST retain the validated service-scope
reference even when no ready lease was published. Missing or contradictory
evidence remains an artifact failure, not inferred success.

The PostgreSQL readiness diagnostic v6 MUST preserve each failed probe as a
bounded typed cause count and the final probe cause separately from window
expiry. A valid SQLSTATE MAY be retained; provider error text MUST NOT be retained.
Before failed-start cleanup, the owner MUST attempt a best-effort container
inspection and bounded startup-log observation under one independent two-second
diagnostic budget. It MUST retain observed state, exit code and OOM status, and
only closed startup milestone/error categories from at most 64 KiB of log data.
Log absence, read failure and truncation MUST remain explicit. Raw logs, paths,
certificate contents and endpoint identities MUST NOT be published. Diagnostic
failure MUST NOT replace the acquisition failure or prevent physical cleanup.
These observations do not extend readiness, authorize retries, or change
admission capacity. Historical v1 records remain historical evidence and MUST
NOT be silently upgraded to v6; the same rule applies to historical v2, v3, v4 and v5 records.

The diagnostic MUST preserve at most 128 ordered startup marker occurrences,
including repeated server-ready events. Events MUST distinguish bootstrap,
final-server and unknown phase using observed initialization boundaries, never
the mere presence of a ready message. Docker-supplied UTC log timestamps and
container-start timestamps MAY supply descriptive elapsed times in the explicitly
labelled Docker wall clock. Missing, malformed, regressing or out-of-range clock
evidence MUST NOT fabricate elapsed values. Log timestamps describe emission,
not the start of an operation whose partial output was buffered. These values
are not canonical monotonic timing and MUST NOT be silently aligned with it.
The existing two-second observation budget, 64 KiB decoded log cap and exact
container binding remain mandatory; framing and marker counts MUST also be
bounded. Truncated partial lines MUST NOT yield complete markers. Failed probe
observations and the first successful SQL connection MUST carry local monotonic
elapsed times relative to acquisition start, with a 128-observation cap and
explicit omission. Observation MUST NOT leave a reader running after cleanup.

Diagnostic v5 MUST bind the selected endpoint, resolver results and actual dial
attempts through bounded per-acquisition opaque references, address families and
address categories. It MUST preserve selection equality, original versus fresh
Docker binding comparisons and exact container identity agreement without retaining
hostnames, addresses, ports, DSNs or provider error text. Resolver and dial observers
MUST delegate the existing driver behavior, preserving order, TLS and errors.
Initial binding observation is best effort, capped at 250 ms within endpoint
resolution; it is an adjacent snapshot, not an atomic witness of port selection.

Failure observation MAY inspect the exact container's internal TCP listener and
attempt TCP transport to the original published endpoint. These are diagnostic
facts, never SQL readiness or permission to substitute another endpoint. Fresh
inspection (250 ms), internal listener observation (500 ms), published transport
(250 ms), state and startup logs share the existing independent two-second budget.
No diagnostic reader may survive cleanup. Address references and binding sets are
capped at 32, resolver/dial observations at 128, and omission is explicit.

Startup log events MUST preserve Docker stdout/stderr provenance and per-stream
line sequence. Timestamp regressions are evaluated within each stream; merged
stream arrival order is not evidence of wall-clock regression. Unknown provenance
remains explicit. Raw stream content is discarded after closed-marker extraction.

On owned PostgreSQL startup failure before ready-binding publication, the exact
acquired allocation has no admitted borrower. Its physical owner SHALL request
zero graceful-stop allowance and perform termination and removal within one fresh
10-second cleanup context, independent of startup cancellation. The zero allowance
SHALL apply only to this unpublished failed-start allocation. Ordinary shutdown
of a successfully published harness SHALL retain its existing graceful-stop
policy. The owner SHALL publish completed settlement only after exact physical
cleanup succeeds. Failed cleanup SHALL preserve the primary acquisition failure,
its separate cleanup outcome, partial ownership, recovery dependencies and resident
claims. This rule SHALL NOT authorize another ordinary cleanup attempt, wider
resource discovery or a replacement startup after SQL readiness has begun.

**Rationale — non-normative:** The container library's ordinary graceful-stop
allowance can exhaust the entire failed-start cleanup budget before removal. An
unpublished allocation has no borrower durability obligation; its bounded cleanup
budget belongs to termination, removal and settlement proof.

An acquired physical resource MUST remain represented by partial ownership or
an explicit completed-settlement receipt on every failed-start path. The generic
startup wrapper MUST NOT discard partial ownership. `startup_failed` describes
the startup outcome and is not physical-settlement proof. Failed cleanup retains
its exact recovery dependencies and resident claims, and cannot authorize another
ordinary cleanup attempt or a replacement service.

Managed startup MUST publish a private, schema-validated startup journal before
helper launch. It binds the exact runtime lease, run, suite, selected services
and resident dependencies. Helper registration, each physical acquisition intent,
returned resource identity, ready publication and physical settlement are distinct
durable states. Concurrent providers MUST serialize journal updates. Acquisition
intent and required cleanup files MUST be recorded before invoking the provider;
returned identity MUST be recorded before starting or exposing the resource.

The startup helper MUST receive cancellation through a private inherited control
channel and register before acquisition. Channel loss cancels startup. Cancellation
fences ready publication and drains late acquisitions into the ordinary physical
cleanup owner. The broker allows at most the existing two-minute cleanup bound
before terminating the exact helper group. Other lifecycle commands retain their
existing cancellation semantics. No ordinary cleanup retry is implied.

Once a managed Docker create request is submitted, cooperative cancellation MUST
drain its response within the original attempt deadline, recording returned identity
before cleanup. Cancellation MUST prevent subsequently starting that container.
A provider timeout with no returned identity remains ambiguous. Preservation MUST
retain its validated bound startup journal even when the ready lease never existed;
preserving this proof is not successful physical settlement.

Recovery MUST validate the startup journal against the original ownership binding.
After helper producers settle, an unstarted journal or explicit completed settlement
can discharge a missing ready lease. An ambiguous provider request, missing lease,
dead helper or empty Docker lookup alone MUST NOT release residency. Valid legacy
leases remain usable; insufficient legacy pending proof remains unresolved.
Once all declared consumers have settled, an acquired owned-container lease is
sufficient physical cleanup authority without its startup environment. Recovery
MUST securely validate its schema, exact original run binding, owned mode, exact
container identities and matching ownership labels, then invoke the existing
physical cleanup owner. It MUST NOT recreate missing environment files or infer
credentials. Missing or invalid leases, borrowed resources and ambiguous pending
acquisitions do not gain this authority. A present but unsafe or malformed recovery
environment remains an error. Resident dependencies are released only after the
physical owner confirms settlement.
Cancellation/readiness and cleanup failures remain independent; recovery summaries
MUST preserve the normalized cleanup-error classification.

Browser owned-stack readiness is an ownership predicate, not only an HTTP availability predicate. The backend is ready only when all of the following hold before the deadline:

- the wrapper-started backend process group is still alive;
- the selected backend port is owned by a process in that process group, when the platform exposes listener process metadata;
- the token-protected `GET /api/v1/test/runtime/identity` route returns `cartulary.test.runtime_identity.v1`, `runtime_marker="harness-owned"`, `test_routes_enabled=true`, and a server process ID;
- the backend process group remains alive after the identity probe.

The canonical browser E2E frontend startup mode is a built preview. Authored
execution topology MUST select one Make-owned artifact for each browser stage:
ordinary stages use the production receipt produced by `build COMPONENT=web`; measurement
uses the measurement receipt produced by `build COMPONENT=web-measurement`. Conventional
`apps/web/dist` and `apps/web/dist-measurement` publications are packaging outputs,
not browser attachment inputs. The selected private build MUST complete and its
`index.html` MUST exist before the preview process starts.
Measurement output contains ordinary application entries and isolated measurement
entries; production and embedded production output MUST exclude measurement entries
and fixture modules. The two artifacts MUST have distinct build/cache identities.
The wrapper MUST launch a non-watching preview against the selected directory.
Missing or invalid built artifacts are `artifact/artifact_error`, exit `11`,
not service-readiness failures.

Browser startup and attachment MUST bind the selected run-relative receipt, its
digest, and the exact content digest using the stack v7 frontend artifact fields. An artifact for a
different stage, a stale or mismatched digest, or an unrecognized path MUST fail
before browser assertions. Artifact selection MUST come from authored topology,
not target-name substring inference or a client query parameter. The ordinary
application MUST NOT expose a debug route as a measurement compatibility path.

Browser probes of independent frontend publication MUST use fresh public build
invocation and artifact identities. They MUST retain the enclosing work unit's
host-admission lease and CPU budget, rather than queue child builds against
capacity already held by their waiting parent. Fresh identity does not require
independent capacity ownership. Execution-result reuse policy MUST remain
explicit. Each child process group MUST be registered with the existing native
runtime owner and settled before fixture teardown; test failure or cancellation
MUST stop those owned children before awaiting their completion. This does not
enlarge browser, build, or cleanup deadlines.

The frontend is ready only when the wrapper-started preview process group is still alive, the selected frontend port is owned by a process in that process group when listener process metadata is available, the frontend HTTP probe succeeds, the process group remains alive after the probe, and stack metadata records `frontend_mode="preview"` and `frontend_command_kind="vite-preview"`. A stale or unrelated listener MUST NOT satisfy browser readiness.

A dynamically allocated browser backend or frontend port lease MUST remain exclusive for the full owned-session lifetime. Before the transient startup controller exits, it MUST transfer each lease to the corresponding live owned process group; the controller exiting MUST NOT make the lease stale while that process group remains alive. A stop controller MAY adopt the exact session's leases, but MUST release them only after it has stopped the recorded process groups and proved the listeners are gone. Allocation MUST reject a lease whose recorded owner is still alive even when the allocating shell that originally created the lease has exited. This ownership transfer and release policy applies across all same-worktree browser schedulers and run roots.

Object-store readiness MUST prove the smallest mutation lifecycle required by
object-backed fixtures, not only port, authentication, or list availability.
The disposable owned object-store fixture MUST explicitly declare its single-master
topology. It MUST NOT wait for an implicit peer quorum when no peer fixtures exist.
This startup configuration does not replace the mutation-readiness contract or
